Matthew 24

1Jesus went out from the temple and was going away, when His disciples came to show Him the temple buildings.

2He answered them, “Do you not see all these things? Truly I tell you, not one stone will be left here upon another that will not be thrown down.”

3As He sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these things happen, and what is the sign of Thy coming and the consummation of the age?”

4Jesus answered them, “See that no one leads you astray.

5For many will come in My name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will lead many astray.

6You will hear wars and reports of wars. See that you are not alarmed, for these things must happen, but the end is not yet.

7For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in various places.

8All these things are the beginning of birth pains.

9Then they will hand you over to affliction and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations because of My name.

10Then many will stumble, hand one another over, and hate one another.

11Many false prophets will arise and lead many astray.

12Because lawlessness increases, the love of many will grow cold.

13But the one who endures to the end will be saved.

14This good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed in the whole inhabited world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.

15So when you see the abomination of desolation spoken of through Daniel the prophet standing in a holy place—let the reader understand—

16then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.

17Let the one on the housetop not go down to take things from his house,

18and let the one in the field not turn back to take his cloak.

19Woe to those with child and those nursing infants in those days!

20Pray that your flight may not occur in winter or on a Sabbath.

21For then there will be great affliction such as has not happened from the beginning of the world until now, and certainly will never happen again.

22If those days had not been shortened, no flesh would have been saved; but because of the chosen, those days will be shortened.

23Then if anyone tells you, ‘Behold, here is the Christ!’ or ‘Here!’ do not believe it.

24For false christs and false prophets will arise and give great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen.

25Behold, I have told you beforehand.

26So if they tell you, ‘Behold, He is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; or ‘Behold, in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.

27For just as lightning comes from the east and shines to the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

28Wherever the corpse is, there the eagles will gather.

29Immediately after the affliction of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its brightness, the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

30Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn; they will see the Son of Man coming upon the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.

31He will send His angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather His chosen from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.

32Learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.

33So also you, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors.

34Truly I tell you that this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things happen.

35Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will certainly not pass away.

36Concerning that day and hour, no one knows, not even the angels of the heavens, nor the Son, but the Father alone.

37For just as the days of Noah were, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

38For in those days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark.

39They did not know until the flood came and took them all away. So also will be the coming of the Son of Man.

40Then two men will be in the field: one is taken and one is left.

41Two women will be grinding at the mill: one is taken and one is left.

42So keep watch, because you do not know on what day your Lord comes.

43But know this: if the householder had known in what watch the thief was coming, he would have kept watch and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.

44Therefore you too must be ready, because the Son of Man comes at an hour you do not expect.

45Who, then, is the faithful and prudent slave whom the master appointed over his household to give them food at the proper time?

46Blessed is that slave whom his master, when he comes, will find doing so.

47Truly I tell you that he will appoint him over all his belongings.

48But if that evil slave says in his heart, ‘My master delays,’

49and begins to beat his fellow slaves and eats and drinks with drunkards,

50the master of that slave will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know.

51He will cut him in two and assign his portion with the hypocrites. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.

Matthew 25

1Then the kingdom of the heavens will be likened to ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.

2Five of them were foolish and five prudent.

3For the foolish took their lamps but did not take oil with them.

4The prudent took oil in containers along with their lamps.

5As the bridegroom delayed, they all became drowsy and slept.

6At midnight a cry arose: ‘Behold, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him.’

7Then all those virgins arose and put their lamps in order.

8The foolish said to the prudent, ‘Give us some of your oil, because our lamps are going out.’

9The prudent answered, ‘There may not be enough for us and you. Go instead to those selling and buy for yourselves.’

10While they went away to buy, the bridegroom came. Those who were ready entered with him into the wedding feast, and the door was shut.

11Afterward the other virgins also came, saying, ‘Lord, lord, open to us.’

12He answered, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’

13Therefore keep watch, because you know neither the day nor the hour.

14For it is like a man traveling abroad, who called his own slaves and handed over his belongings to them.

15To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, each according to his own ability, and traveled abroad. Immediately

16the one who received the five talents went and traded with them and gained another five.

17Likewise the one with two gained another two.

18But the one who received one went away, dug in the ground, and hid his master’s silver.

19After a long time, the master of those slaves came and settled accounts with them.

20The one who received five talents came and brought another five talents, saying, ‘Master, you handed over five talents to me. Look, I gained another five talents.’

21His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful slave. You were faithful over a few things; I will appoint you over many. Enter into your master’s joy.’

22The one with two talents also came and said, ‘Master, you handed over two talents to me. Look, I gained another two talents.’

23His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful slave. You were faithful over a few things; I will appoint you over many. Enter into your master’s joy.’

24The one who received one talent also came and said, ‘Master, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering from where you did not scatter.

25I was afraid, so I went away and hid your talent in the ground. Look, you have what is yours.’

26His master answered him, ‘Evil and idle slave! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather from where I did not scatter?

27Then you ought to have deposited my silver with the bankers, and when I came I would have recovered what is mine with interest.

28So take the talent from him and give it to the one who has the ten talents.

29For to everyone who has, more will be given and he will have abundance; but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken.

30Cast the useless slave into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.’

31When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, then He will sit upon the throne of His glory.

32All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them from one another as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.

33He will stand the sheep at His right and the young goats at His left.

34Then the King will say to those at His right, ‘Come, you blessed by My Father; inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.

35For I was hungry and you gave Me food, I was thirsty and you gave Me drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed Me,

36naked and you clothed Me, I was sick and you visited Me, I was in prison and you came to Me.’

37Then the righteous will answer Him, ‘Lord, when did we see Thee hungry and feed Thee, or thirsty and give Thee drink?

38When did we see Thee a stranger and welcome Thee, or naked and clothe Thee?

39When did we see Thee sick or in prison and come to Thee?’

40The King will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did it to one of the least of these My brothers, you did it to Me.’

41Then He will also say to those at His left, ‘Depart from Me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

42For I was hungry and you did not give Me food, I was thirsty and you did not give Me drink,

43I was a stranger and you did not welcome Me, naked and you did not clothe Me, sick and in prison and you did not visit Me.’

44Then they too will answer, ‘Lord, when did we see Thee hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not serve Thee?’

45Then He will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did not do it to one of the least of these, neither did you do it to Me.’

46And these shall depart into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

Matthew 26

1When Jesus finished all these words, He said to His disciples,

2“You know that after two days the Passover takes place, and the Son of Man is handed over to be crucified.”

3Then the chief priests and elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest called Caiaphas.

4They took counsel to seize Jesus by deceit and kill Him.

5But they said, “Not during the feast, lest an uproar occur among the people.”

6While Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,

7a woman came to Him with an alabaster flask of very costly perfume and poured it upon His head as He reclined at table.

8Seeing it, the disciples became indignant, saying, “Why this waste?

9For this could have been sold for much and given to the poor.”

10Knowing this, Jesus said to them, “Why do you trouble the woman? For she has done a good work toward Me.

11For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have Me.

12By pouring this perfume upon My body, she did it to prepare Me for burial.

13Truly I tell you, wherever this good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she did will also be told in remembrance of her.”

14Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests

15and said, “What are you willing to give me, and I will hand Him over to you?” They weighed out for him thirty silver coins.

16From then on he sought a suitable opportunity to hand Him over.

17On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus, saying, “Where dost Thou wish us to prepare for Thee to eat the Passover?”

18He said, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The Teacher says: My appointed time is near. I keep the Passover at your house with My disciples.’”

19The disciples did as Jesus directed them, and prepared the Passover.

20When evening came, He reclined at table with the twelve.

21As they ate, He said, “Truly I tell you that one of you will hand Me over.”

22Exceedingly grieved, each began saying to Him, “Surely it is not I, Lord?”

23He answered, “The one who dipped his hand with Me in the dish will hand Me over.

24The Son of Man indeed goes as it is written concerning Him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would have been good for him if that man had not been born.”

25Judas, who was handing Him over, answered, “Surely it is not I, Rabbi?” He said to him, “You have said it.”

26And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and having blessed, He broke it; and giving it to the disciples, He said, “Take, eat; this is My body.”

27And He took a cup, and having given thanks, He gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you;

28for this is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for forgiveness of sins.

29And I tell you: from this time I shall by no means drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of My Father.”

30After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

31Then Jesus said to them, “All of you will stumble because of Me this night, for it is written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’

32But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”

33Peter answered Him, “Even if everyone stumbles because of Thee, I will never stumble.”

34Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you that this night, before a rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.”

35Peter said to Him, “Even if I must die with Thee, I will certainly not deny Thee.” All the disciples said likewise.

36Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and said to the disciples, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”

37Taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, He began to be grieved and distressed.

38Then He said to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, even to death. Remain here and keep watch with Me.”

39Going forward a little, He fell upon His face and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me. Nevertheless, not as I wish, but as Thou wishest.”

40He came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “So, could you not keep watch with Me for one hour?

41Keep watch and pray, so that you may not enter temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

42Again He went away a second time and prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cannot pass unless I drink it, let Thy will be done.”

43He came and again found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.

44He left them and went away again, praying a third time and saying the same words again.

45Then He came to the disciples and said to them, “Sleep on now and rest. Behold, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man is handed over into sinners’ hands.

46Rise, let us go. Behold, the one handing Me over has drawn near.”

47While He was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came with a great crowd carrying swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.

48The one handing Him over had given them a sign, saying, “The One I kiss is He; seize Him.”

49Immediately he came to Jesus and said, “Greetings, Rabbi,” and kissed Him.

50Jesus said to him, “Friend, do what you have come for.” Then they came forward, laid their hands upon Jesus, and seized Him.

51And behold, one of those with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, struck the high priest’s slave, and cut off his ear.

52Then Jesus said to him, “Return your sword to its place, for all who take a sword will perish by a sword.

53Or do you think I cannot plead with My Father, and He will provide Me at once more than twelve legions of angels?

54How, then, would the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen this way?”

55At that hour Jesus said to the crowds, “Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs, to arrest Me? Daily I sat teaching in the temple, and you did not seize Me.

56But all this has happened so that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples left Him and fled.

57Those who seized Jesus led Him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.

58Peter followed Him at a distance as far as the high priest’s courtyard. Going inside, he sat with the officers to see the outcome.

59The chief priests and the whole council sought false testimony against Jesus to put Him to death,

60but found none, although many false witnesses came forward. Finally two came forward

61and said, “This Man said, ‘I can destroy God’s sanctuary and build it in three days.’”

62The high priest rose and said to Him, “Dost Thou answer nothing? What is this that they testify against Thee?”

63But Jesus remained silent. The high priest said to Him, “I adjure Thee by the living God to tell us whether Thou art the Christ, the Son of God.”

64Jesus said to him, “You have said it. Nevertheless I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right of the Power and coming upon the clouds of heaven.”

65Then the high priest tore his garments, saying, “He has blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses? Look, now you heard the blasphemy.

66What do you think?” They answered, “He is liable to death.”

67Then they spat into His face and struck Him with their fists; others slapped Him,

68saying, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who is the one who struck Thee?”

69Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. One servant girl approached him, saying, “You too were with Jesus the Galilean.”

70But he denied it before everyone, saying, “I do not know what you are saying.”

71When he went out to the gateway, another girl saw him and said to those there, “This man was with Jesus the Nazarene.”

72Again he denied it with an oath: “I do not know the Man.”

73After a little while, those standing there came and said to Peter, “Truly you too are one of them, for even your speech makes you recognizable.”

74Then he began to invoke curses and swear, “I do not know the Man.” Immediately a rooster crowed.

75Peter remembered Jesus’ word: “Before a rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.” He went outside and wept bitterly.

Matthew 27

1When morning came, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put Him to death.

2They bound Him, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate the governor.

3Then Judas, who had handed Him over, saw that He had been condemned. Filled with regret, he returned the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and elders,

4saying, “I sinned by handing over innocent blood.” They said, “What is that to us? See to it yourself.”

5He threw the silver coins into the sanctuary and withdrew; then he went away and hanged himself.

6The chief priests took the silver coins and said, “It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, because they are the price of blood.”

7After taking counsel, they bought the potter’s field with them as a burial place for strangers.

8Therefore that field has been called Field of Blood until today.

9Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled: “They took the thirty silver coins, the price of the One priced, whom some of the sons of Israel priced,

10and gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord directed me.”

11Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned Him, saying, “Art Thou the King of the Jews?” Jesus said, “You say it.”

12While He was accused by the chief priests and elders, He answered nothing.

13Then Pilate said to Him, “Dost Thou not hear how many things they testify against Thee?”

14He did not answer him even one word, so that the governor marveled greatly.

15At the feast the governor customarily released to the crowd one prisoner whom they wanted.

16At that time they had a notorious prisoner called Jesus Barabbas.

17So when they gathered, Pilate said to them, “Whom do you want me to release to you: Jesus Barabbas, or Jesus called Christ?”

18For he knew that they had handed Him over because of envy.

19While he sat on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying, “Have nothing to do with that righteous Man, for I suffered many things today in a dream because of Him.”

20But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and destroy Jesus.

21The governor answered them, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” They said, “Barabbas.”

22Pilate said to them, “What then shall I do with Jesus called Christ?” They all said, “Let Him be crucified!”

23He said, “Why, what evil did He do?” But they cried out all the more, “Let Him be crucified!”

24When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but rather an uproar was arising, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying, “I am innocent of this blood. See to it yourselves.”

25All the people answered, “His blood be upon us and upon our children.”

26Then he released Barabbas to them; after flogging Jesus, he handed Him over to be crucified.

27Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort around Him.

28They stripped Him and put a scarlet cloak around Him.

29They wove a crown from thorns, placed it upon His head, and put a reed in His right hand. Kneeling before Him, they mocked Him, saying, “Greetings, King of the Jews!”

30They spat on Him, took the reed, and kept striking Him upon the head.

31After mocking Him, they stripped off the cloak, dressed Him in His own garments, and led Him away to crucify Him.

32As they went out, they found a Cyrenian man named Simon. They compelled him to carry His cross.

33They came to a place called Golgotha, which is called Place of a Skull,

34and gave Him wine mixed with gall to drink. After tasting it, He was unwilling to drink.

35After crucifying Him, they divided His garments by casting a lot,

36and sat there keeping watch over Him.

37Above His head they placed the written charge against Him: “This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.”

38Then two robbers were crucified with Him, one at His right and one at His left.

39Those passing by reviled Him, shaking their heads

40and saying, “Thou who destroyest the sanctuary and buildest it in three days, save Thyself! If Thou art God’s Son, come down from the cross.”

41Likewise the chief priests, mocking with the scribes and elders, said,

42“He saved others; Himself He cannot save. He is King of Israel! Let Him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in Him.

43He trusts in God; let Him rescue Him now, if He desires Him, for He said, ‘I am God’s Son.’”

44The robbers crucified with Him also reproached Him in the same way.

45From the sixth hour darkness came upon all the land until the ninth hour.

46And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” That is, “My God, My God, why hast Thou forsaken Me?”

47Some standing there heard and said, “This Man is calling Elijah.”

48Immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, placed it on a reed, and gave Him a drink.

49But the rest said, “Leave it; let us see whether Elijah comes to save Him.”

50Jesus again cried out with a loud voice and released His spirit.

51And behold, the veil of the sanctuary was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, and the rocks split.

52The tombs were opened, and many bodies of the holy ones who had fallen asleep were raised.

53Coming out of the tombs after His rising, they entered the holy city and appeared to many.

54The centurion and those with him guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and what had happened, and were exceedingly afraid, saying, “Truly this was God’s Son.”

55Many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving Him.

56Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.

57When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph came, who himself had also become Jesus’ disciple.

58He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate ordered it to be given.

59Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.

60He laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut in the rock. Rolling a great stone to the tomb’s entrance, he went away.

61Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.

62On the next day, which was after the Preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees gathered before Pilate,

63saying, “Sir, we remembered that while He was still alive, that deceiver said, ‘After three days I am raised.’

64So command that the tomb be made secure until the third day, lest His disciples come, steal Him, and tell the people, ‘He has been raised from the dead,’ and the last deception will be worse than the first.”

65Pilate said to them, “You have a guard. Go and make it secure as you know how.”

66They went and secured the tomb by sealing the stone, with the guard.

Mark 1

1The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, Son of God.

2As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Look, I send My messenger before Thy face, who will prepare Thy way;

3a voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make His paths straight.’”

4John appeared, baptizing in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.

5The whole Judean countryside and all the people of Jerusalem were going out to him. They were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.

6John was clothed in camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and ate locusts and wild honey.

7He proclaimed, saying, “The One stronger than I is coming after me. I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the strap of His sandals.

8I baptized you with water, but He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.”

9In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized in the Jordan by John.

10Immediately as He came up out of the water, He saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit descending like a dove into Him.

11A voice came from the heavens: “Thou art My beloved Son; in Thee I am well pleased.”

12Immediately the Spirit drove Him out into the wilderness.

13He was in the wilderness forty days, being tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and the angels ministered to Him.

14And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the gospel of God,

15and saying, “The appointed time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near; repent, and believe in the gospel.”

16And passing beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting a net in the sea, for they were fishermen.

17And He said to them, “Come after Me, and I will make you become fishers of men.”

18Immediately they left their nets and followed Him.

19Going a little farther, He saw James son of Zebedee and John his brother, who were also in the boat, putting the nets in order.

20Immediately He called them. They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers and went after Him.

21They entered Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath He went into the synagogue and taught.

22They were astonished at His teaching, for He taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.

23Immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,

24“What have we to do with Thee, Jesus of Nazareth? Hast Thou come to destroy us? I know who Thou art—the Holy One of God!”

25Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be muzzled, and come out of him!”

26The unclean spirit convulsed him, cried out with a loud voice, and came out of him.

27They were all amazed, so that they discussed among themselves, saying, “What is this? A new teaching! With authority He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him.”

28Immediately the report about Him went out everywhere through the whole surrounding region of Galilee.

29Immediately after leaving the synagogue, they went into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.

30Simon’s mother-in-law was lying down with a fever, and immediately they told Him about her.

31He came to her, took her by the hand, and raised her up. The fever left her, and she served them.

32When evening came, after the sun had set, they brought to Him all who were ill and those possessed by demons.

33The whole city had gathered at the door.

34He healed many who were ill with various diseases and cast out many demons. He would not allow the demons to speak, because they knew Him.

35Very early, while it was still dark, He arose, went out, and departed to a deserted place, and there He prayed.

36Simon and those with him searched for Him

37and found Him. They said to Him, “Everyone is looking for Thee.”

38He said to them, “Let us go elsewhere, into the neighboring towns, so that I may proclaim there also, for that is why I came out.”

39He went throughout all Galilee, proclaiming in their synagogues and casting out the demons.

40A leper came to Him, pleading with Him, kneeling, and saying, “If Thou art willing, Thou canst cleanse me.”

41And moved with compassion, He stretched out His hand and touched him, and says to him, “I will; be cleansed.”

42Immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed.

43Sternly warning him, He immediately drove him away

44and said to him, “See that you say nothing to anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”

45But he went out and began proclaiming it widely and spreading the report, so that Jesus could no longer enter a city openly. He remained outside in deserted places, and they came to Him from every direction.

Mark 2

1When He entered Capernaum again after some days, it was heard that He was at home.

2Many gathered, so that there was no longer room, not even near the door, and He was speaking the word to them.

5Jesus saw their faith and said to the paralyzed man, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”

6Some of the scribes were sitting there and reasoning in their hearts,

7“Why does this man speak this way? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins except the one God?”

8Immediately Jesus knew in His spirit that they were reasoning this way within themselves. He said to them, “Why are you reasoning these things in your hearts?

9Which is easier: to say to the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Arise, take your mat, and walk’?

10But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—He said to the paralyzed man—

11“I say to you, arise, take your mat, and go to your house.”

12He arose, immediately took up the mat, and went out before everyone. They were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”

13He went out again beside the sea. The whole crowd came to Him, and He taught them.

14As He passed by, He saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax station. He said to him, “Follow Me.” He arose and followed Him.

15As He reclined at table in his house, many tax collectors and sinners reclined with Jesus and His disciples, for there were many who followed Him.

16The scribes of the Pharisees saw that He was eating with sinners and tax collectors and said to His disciples, “Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

17Jesus heard and said to them, “The strong have no need of a physician, but those who are ill do. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”

18John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. They came and said to Him, “Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but Thy disciples do not fast?”

19Jesus said to them, “Can the bridegroom’s companions fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

20But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast on that day.

21No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment. Otherwise the new patch pulls away from the old, and a worse tear results.

22No one puts new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is lost along with the skins. New wine belongs in fresh wineskins.”

23He was passing through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and His disciples began to make their way, plucking the heads of grain.

24The Pharisees said to Him, “Look! Why are they doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”

25He said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those with him:

26how he entered God’s house in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the loaves of presentation, which only priests may lawfully eat, and also gave them to those who were with him?”

27And He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Sabbath.

28So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”

Mark 4

1Again He began teaching beside the sea. A very great crowd gathered around Him, so that He got into a boat on the sea and sat down, while the whole crowd was on the land beside the sea.

5Other seed fell on rocky ground, where it had little soil, and immediately sprang up because the soil had no depth.

6When the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no root, it withered.

7Other seed fell among the thorns. The thorns grew up and choked it, and it gave no fruit.

8Other seeds fell into the good soil and gave fruit, growing up and increasing; they yielded thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.”

9He said, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”

10When He was alone, those around Him, together with the Twelve, asked Him about the parables.

11He said to them, “To you the mystery of the kingdom of God has been given. But for those outside, everything comes in parables,

12so that, looking, they may look and not see, and hearing, they may hear and not understand, lest they turn back and be forgiven.”

13He said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? Then how will you understand all the parables?

14The sower sows the word.

15These are the ones beside the road where the word is sown: whenever they hear, Satan immediately comes and takes away the word sown into them.

16Likewise, these are the ones sown on the rocky places: whenever they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy,

17but they have no root in themselves and last only for a time. Then, when distress or persecution comes because of the word, they immediately stumble.

18Others are the ones sown among the thorns. These are the ones who have heard the word,

19but the cares of the age, the deceitfulness of riches, and desires for other things enter and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.

20Those sown on the good soil are the ones who hear the word, accept it, and bear fruit: thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.”

21He said to them, “Does the lamp come to be put under the modius basket, or under the bed? Is it not to be put on the lampstand?

22For nothing is hidden except to be revealed, nor has anything become secret except to come into the open.

10He begged Him earnestly not to send them out of the country.

11Now a large herd of pigs was feeding there near the mountain.

12They begged Him, saying, “Send us into the pigs, so that we may enter them.”

13He allowed them. The unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea—about two thousand—and they drowned in the sea.

14Those tending them fled and reported it in the city and in the fields. People came to see what had happened.

15They came to Jesus and saw the demon-possessed man sitting, clothed and in his right mind—the one who had had the legion—and they were afraid.

16Those who had seen it told them what had happened to the demon-possessed man and about the pigs.

19He did not allow him, but said to him, “Go home to your own people and report to them how much the Lord has done for you and how He has had mercy on you.”

23and begged Him earnestly, saying, “My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come and lay Thy hands on her, so that she may be saved and live.”

24He went with him. A large crowd followed Him and pressed against Him.

25A woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years,

26and had suffered much under many physicians and spent everything she had, without any benefit but instead growing worse,

27heard about Jesus. She came behind Him in the crowd and touched His garment.

29Immediately the source of her blood dried up, and she knew in her body that she was healed of the affliction.

30Immediately Jesus, recognizing in Himself that power had gone out from Him, turned around in the crowd and said, “Who touched My clothes?”

31His disciples said to Him, “Thou seest the crowd pressing against Thee, and Thou sayest, ‘Who touched Me?’”

32He kept looking around to see the woman who had done this.

33The woman, afraid and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell before Him and told Him the whole truth.

34And He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace, and be well, free from your affliction.”

35While He was still speaking, people came from the synagogue ruler’s house, saying, “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the Teacher any further?”

37He allowed no one to accompany Him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.

38They came to the synagogue ruler’s house, and He saw a commotion, with people weeping and wailing loudly.

39He went in and said to them, “Why are you making a commotion and weeping? The child has not died but is sleeping.”

41Taking the child’s hand, He said to her, “Talitha koum,” which translated means, “Little girl, I say to you, arise!”

42Immediately the little girl rose and walked around, for she was twelve years old. Immediately they were overcome with great amazement.

1He left there and came to His hometown, and His disciples followed Him.

9but to wear sandals, and, “Do not put on two tunics.”

10He said to them, “Wherever you enter a house, remain there until you leave that place.

11Whatever place does not receive you, and whose people do not listen to you, shake off the dust beneath your feet as you leave there, as a testimony to them.”

12They went out and proclaimed that people should repent.

13They cast out many demons, and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.

14King Herod heard of it, for His name had become known. People were saying, “John the baptizer has been raised from the dead, and that is why mighty powers are at work in Him.”

15Others said, “He is Elijah.” Still others said, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets.”

16But when Herod heard, he said, “John, whom I beheaded—he has been raised!”

17For Herod himself had sent men to seize John and bind him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, because he had married her.

18For John had been saying to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”

19Herodias held a grudge against him and wanted to kill him, but she could not.

20For Herod feared John, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he was greatly perplexed, yet he listened to him gladly.

21An opportune day came when Herod gave a dinner on his birthday for his dignitaries, commanders of thousands, and the leading men of Galilee.

22His daughter Herodias came in and danced, pleasing Herod and those reclining with him. The king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”

23He swore to her repeatedly, “Whatever you ask of me, I will give you, up to half my kingdom.”

24She went out and said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” She said, “The head of John the baptizer.”

25Immediately she hurried in to the king and made her request, saying, “I want you to give me at once, on a platter, the head of John the Baptist.”

26The king became deeply grieved, but because of his oaths and those reclining at table, he did not want to refuse her.

27Immediately the king sent an executioner and ordered him to bring John’s head. He went and beheaded him in prison,

28brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the girl; the girl gave it to her mother.

29When his disciples heard, they came and took his corpse and laid it in a tomb.

30The apostles gathered around Jesus and reported to Him everything they had done and taught.

31He said to them, “Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little.” For many were coming and going, and they did not even have an opportunity to eat.

32They went away privately in the boat to a deserted place.

33People saw them leaving, and many recognized them. They ran there together on foot from all the cities and arrived ahead of them.

34As He stepped out, He saw a large crowd and was moved with compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. He began teaching them many things.

35When the hour was already late, His disciples came to Him and said, “The place is deserted, and the hour is already late.

36Dismiss them, so that they can go into the surrounding fields and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”

37He answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They said to Him, “Should we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them something to eat?”

38He said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” When they found out, they said, “Five, and two fish.”

39He ordered them to have everyone recline in dining groups on the green grass.

40They reclined in rows, by hundreds and by fifties.

41He took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, pronounced a blessing, and broke the loaves. He kept giving them to His disciples to set before the people, and He divided the two fish among them all.

42They all ate and were satisfied.

43They took up broken pieces, twelve baskets full, and some of the fish.

44Those who had eaten the loaves were five thousand men.

45Immediately He compelled His disciples to board the boat and go ahead to the other side, toward Bethsaida, while He Himself dismissed the crowd.

46After saying farewell to them, He went away to the mountain to pray.

47When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and He was alone on the land.

48Seeing them straining at the rowing, for the wind was against them, He came toward them about the fourth watch of the night, walking on the sea. He intended to pass by them.

49When they saw Him walking on the sea, they thought it was a phantom and cried out,

50for they all saw Him and were troubled. Immediately He spoke with them and said to them, “Take courage! It is I; do not fear.”

51He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind ceased. They were utterly astounded within themselves,

52for they had not understood about the loaves, but their heart was hardened.

55and ran through that whole country. They began carrying the sick around on their mats to wherever they heard He was.

1The Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Him.

7In vain do they worship Me, teaching human commands for doctrine.’

9He said to them, “You set aside God’s commandment very well indeed, so that you may establish your tradition!

10For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Let whoever speaks evil of father or mother surely die.’

11But you say, ‘If a person says to his father or mother, “Whatever benefit you might receive from me is Corban”—that is, a gift—’

12you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or mother,

13making void the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down. You do many similar things.”

14Calling the crowd to Him again, He said to them, “Listen to Me, all of you, and understand.

15There is nothing outside a person that, by entering him, can defile him. Rather, the things coming out of a person are what defile the person.”

18He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not grasp that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile him,

19because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—thus cleansing all foods.

20He said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles the person.

21For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil reasonings, acts of sexual immorality, thefts, murders,

22adulteries, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness.

23All these evil things come out from within and defile the person.”

24He rose from there and went away into the territory of Tyre. He entered a house and wanted no one to know, but He could not remain hidden.

25Immediately a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit heard about Him, came, and fell at His feet.

26The woman was Greek, Syrophoenician by birth. She asked Him to cast the demon out of her daughter.

27He said to her, “Let the children first be satisfied, for it is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the little dogs.”

28She answered and said to Him, “Lord, even the little dogs under the table eat some of the children’s crumbs.”

29He said to her, “Because of this word, go; the demon has gone out of your daughter.”

30She went home and found the child lying on the bed, and the demon gone.

31Leaving the territory of Tyre again, He came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the middle of the territory of the Decapolis.

32They brought Him a man who was deaf and had difficulty speaking, and begged Him to lay His hand on him.

33Taking him aside privately, away from the crowd, He put His fingers into his ears, spat, and touched his tongue.

34Looking up to heaven, He sighed and said to him, “Ephphatha,” that is, “Be opened.”

35Immediately his ears were opened, the bond of his tongue was loosened, and he spoke correctly.

36He ordered them to tell no one. But the more He ordered them, the more abundantly they proclaimed it.

37They were astonished beyond measure, saying, “He has done everything well! He even makes the deaf hear and the speechless speak.”

11He said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.

12And if she divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.”

13People brought children to Him so that He might touch them, but the disciples rebuked them.

14When Jesus saw it, He was indignant and said to them, “Let the children come to Me; do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

15Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will certainly not enter it.”

16He embraced them and blessed them, laying His hands on them.

17As He was setting out on the road, a man ran up, knelt before Him, and asked Him, “Good Teacher, what should I do to inherit eternal life?”

18Jesus said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good except One—God.

19You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder; do not commit adultery; do not steal; do not bear false witness; do not defraud; honor your father and mother.’”

20He said to Him, “Teacher, I have kept all these from my youth.”

21Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “You lack one thing. Go, sell what you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”

22But his face fell at the word, and he went away grieved, for he had many possessions.

23Jesus looked around and said to His disciples, “How hard it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!”

24The disciples were astounded at His words. But Jesus answered them again, “Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!

25It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”

26They were exceedingly astonished and said to one another, “Then who can be saved?”

27Jesus looked at them and said, “With humans it is impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God.”

28Peter began saying to Him, “Look, we have left everything and followed Thee.”

29Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, brothers, sisters, mother, father, children, or fields for My sake and for the sake of the gospel,

30who will not receive a hundredfold now, in this time—houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and fields, with persecutions—and in the coming age, eternal life.

31But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

32They were on the road going up to Jerusalem. Jesus was going ahead of them, and they were astounded, while those following were afraid. Taking the Twelve aside again, He began telling them what was going to happen to Him:

33“Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn Him to death and hand Him over to the Gentiles.

34They will mock Him, spit on Him, flog Him, and kill Him, and after three days He will rise.”

35James and John, the sons of Zebedee, approached Him and said to Him, “Teacher, we want Thee to do for us whatever we ask Thee.”

36He said to them, “What do you want Me to do for you?”

37They said to Him, “Grant us to sit, one at Thy right and one at Thy left, in Thy glory.”

38Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”

39They said to Him, “We can.” Jesus said to them, “You will drink the cup that I drink, and you will be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized.

40But to sit at My right or at My left is not Mine to give; it is for those for whom it has been prepared.”

41When the ten heard, they began to be indignant with James and John.

42Jesus called them to Him and said to them, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.

43But it is not so among you. Whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant,

44and whoever wants to be first among you shall be slave of all.

45For even the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom in exchange for many.”

46They came to Jericho. As He was leaving Jericho with His disciples and a considerable crowd, Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.

47Hearing that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began crying out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”

48Many rebuked him so that he would be silent, but he cried out much more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

49Jesus stopped and said, “Call him.” They called the blind man, saying to him, “Take courage! Get up; He is calling you.”

50He threw off his garment, sprang up, and came to Jesus.

51Jesus answered him, “What do you want Me to do for you?” The blind man said to Him, “Rabbouni, that I may see again.”

52Jesus said to him, “Go; your faith has saved you.” Immediately he saw again and followed Him on the road.

Mark 11

1As they drew near Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, He sent two of His disciples

2and said to them, “Go into the village opposite you. Immediately on entering it, you will find a colt tied, on which no human has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.

3If anyone says to you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say, ‘The Lord has need of it, and He will send it back here immediately.’”

4They went away and found a colt tied at a door outside on the street, and untied it.

5Some of those standing there said to them, “What are you doing, untying the colt?”

6They answered them just as Jesus had said, and the people let them go.

7They brought the colt to Jesus, threw their garments on it, and He sat on it.

8Many spread their garments on the road; others spread leafy branches they had cut from the fields.

9Those going ahead and those following cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord!

10Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!”

11He entered Jerusalem, into the temple. After looking around at everything, since the hour was already late, He went out to Bethany with the Twelve.

12On the next day, as they came out from Bethany, He became hungry.

13Seeing from far away a fig tree with leaves, He came to see whether He might find anything on it. When He reached it, He found nothing but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.

14He addressed it, “May no one ever eat fruit from you again.” His disciples heard it.

15They came to Jerusalem. He entered the temple and began driving out those selling and those buying in the temple. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves,

16and would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple.

17He taught and said to them, “Is it not written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers.”

18The chief priests and the scribes heard, and sought how to destroy Him; for they feared Him, because the whole crowd was astonished at His teaching.

19Whenever evening came, they went out of the city.

20Passing by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.

21Peter remembered and said to Him, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree that Thou didst curse has withered.”

22Jesus answered them, “Have faith in God.

23Truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says is happening, it will be his.

24Therefore I tell you, everything you pray and ask for—believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.

25Whenever you stand praying, forgive if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father in the heavens may also forgive your trespasses.”

27They came again to Jerusalem. As He walked in the temple, the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders came to Him

28and said to Him, “By what authority art Thou doing these things? Or who gave Thee this authority to do them?”

29Jesus said to them, “I will ask you one question. Answer Me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.

30Was John’s baptism from heaven or from humans? Answer Me.”

31They reasoned with one another, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

32But should we say, ‘From humans’?” They feared the crowd, for everyone held that John truly was a prophet.

33They answered Jesus, “We do not know.” Jesus said to them, “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

Mark 12

1He began speaking to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress vat, and built a tower. He leased it to tenant farmers and went abroad.

2At the proper season he sent a slave to the farmers, to receive from them some of the vineyard’s fruit.

3They seized him, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.

4Again he sent another slave to them; they struck that one on the head and dishonored him.

5He sent another, and they killed that one; and many others—some they beat, and others they killed.

6He still had one, a beloved son. He sent him to them last, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’

7But those farmers said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’

8They seized him, killed him, and threw him outside the vineyard.

9What, then, will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers and give the vineyard to others.

10Have you not even read this Scripture: ‘The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.

11This came from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”

12They sought to seize Him, but feared the crowd, for they knew that He had spoken the parable against them. They left Him and went away.

13They sent some of the Pharisees and the Herodians to Him, to catch Him in a word.

14They came and said to Him, “Teacher, we know that Thou art truthful and dost not defer to anyone, for Thou dost not look at people’s outward standing, but dost teach God’s way in truth. Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar or not? Should we give it or not?”

15Knowing their hypocrisy, He said to them, “Why are you testing Me? Bring Me a denarius so that I may see it.”

16They brought one. He said to them, “Whose image and inscription is this?” They said to Him, “Caesar’s.”

17Jesus said to them, “Give back Caesar’s things to Caesar, and God’s things to God.” They marveled greatly at Him.

18Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Him and questioned Him, saying,

19“Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if someone’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no child, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.

20There were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and died leaving no offspring.

21The second took her and died leaving no offspring, and the third likewise.

22The seven left no offspring. Last of all, the woman also died.

23In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? For the seven had her as wife.”

24Jesus said to them, “Is this not why you are mistaken: you know neither the Scriptures nor God’s power?

25For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in the heavens.

26As for the dead being raised, have you not read in the book of Moses, in the passage about the bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob’?

27He is not God of the dead, but of the living. You are greatly mistaken.”

28One of the scribes approached, having heard them disputing and seen that He had answered them well. He asked Him, “Which commandment is first of all?”

29Jesus answered, “The first is, ‘Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.

30You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, with your whole soul, with your whole mind, and with your whole strength.’

31The second is this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”

32The scribe said to Him, “Well said, Teacher! Thou hast truly said that He is one, and there is no other besides Him.

33To love Him with the whole heart, with the whole understanding, and with the whole strength, and to love one’s neighbor as oneself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”

34Seeing that he answered thoughtfully, Jesus said to him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” No one dared to question Him any further.

35Jesus responded as He taught in the temple, “How do the scribes say that the Christ is David’s son?

36David himself said in the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at My right hand until I put Thy enemies beneath Thy feet.’

37David himself calls Him Lord; how then is He his son?” The large crowd listened to Him gladly.

38In His teaching He said, “Beware of the scribes who like to walk about in long robes and receive greetings in the marketplaces,

39the foremost seats in the synagogues, and the foremost reclining places at dinners.

40They devour widows’ houses and make long prayers as a pretense. These will receive greater judgment.”

41He sat opposite the treasury and watched how the crowd put copper money into the treasury. Many rich people put in much.

42And one poor widow came and put in two lepta, which make a quadrans.

43He called His disciples to Him and said to them, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all those putting into the treasury.

44For they all put in from their surplus, but she, from her need, put in everything she had—her whole livelihood.”

Mark 13

1As He was leaving the temple, one of His disciples said to Him, “Teacher, look! What stones and what buildings!”

2Jesus said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left here on another that will not be torn down.”

3As He sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew questioned Him privately:

4“Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be fulfilled?”

5Jesus began saying to them, “Watch out that no one leads you astray.

6Many will come in My name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and will lead many astray.

7When you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be alarmed. These must happen, but the end is not yet.

8For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places; there will be famines. These things are the beginning of birth pains.

9But watch yourselves. They will hand you over to councils; you will be beaten in synagogues, and you will stand before governors and kings for My sake, as a testimony to them.

10The gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.

11When they lead you away to hand you over, do not worry beforehand about what to say. Whatever is given you in that hour, say that; for it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.

12Brother will hand brother over to death, and a father his child. Children will rise against parents and have them put to death.

13You will be hated by all because of My name. But the one who endures to the end will be saved.

14When you see the abomination of desolation standing where it must not—let the reader understand—then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.

15Let the one on the housetop not go down or enter to take anything from his house,

16and let the one in the field not turn back to take his garment.

17Woe to those who are pregnant and those nursing infants in those days!

18Pray that it does not happen in winter.

19For those days will be distress such as has not occurred from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, and certainly will not occur again.

20If the Lord had not shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved. But for the sake of the chosen, whom He chose, He shortened the days.

21Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ do not believe it.

22For false christs and false prophets will arise and give signs and wonders to lead astray, if possible, the chosen.

23But you, watch out! I have told you everything beforehand.

24But in those days, after that distress, the sun will be darkened and the moon will not give its light.

25The stars will be falling from heaven, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.

26Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.

27Then He will send the angels and gather His chosen from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.

28Learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.

29So also, when you see these things happening, know that it is near, at the doors.

30Truly I tell you, this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things happen.

31Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will certainly not pass away.

32But concerning that day or hour, no one knows—not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son—except the Father.

33Watch out; stay awake, for you do not know when the time is.

34It is like a man going abroad who left his house and gave his slaves authority, each his own work, and commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.

35Therefore keep watch, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming: in the evening, at midnight, at cockcrow, or in the morning.

36Otherwise he may come suddenly and find you sleeping.

37What I say to you, I say to all: keep watch!”

Mark 14

1The Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away. The chief priests and the scribes sought how to seize Him by deceit and kill Him.

2For they said, “Not during the feast, lest there be a disturbance among the people.”

3While He was in Bethany, reclining in the house of Simon the leper, a woman came with an alabaster jar of very costly ointment of pure nard. She broke the alabaster jar and poured it over His head.

4Some were indignant among themselves: “Why has this ointment been wasted?

5For this ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor.” They scolded her harshly.

6Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why are you troubling her? She has done a good work for Me.

7For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want, you can do good to them; but you do not always have Me.

8She did what she could. She has anointed My body beforehand for burial.

9Truly I tell you, wherever the gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in remembrance of her.”

10Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went away to the chief priests to hand Him over to them.

11When they heard, they rejoiced and promised to give him silver money. He sought how to hand Him over at a suitable time.

12On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they sacrificed the Passover, His disciples said to Him, “Where dost Thou want us to go and prepare the Passover for Thee to eat?”

13He sent two of His disciples and said to them, “Go into the city, and a man carrying an earthenware jar of water will meet you. Follow him.

14Wherever he enters, say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says: Where is My guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’

15He will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready. Prepare for us there.”

16The disciples went out, came to the city, and found it just as He had told them. They prepared the Passover.

17When evening came, He arrived with the Twelve.

18As they reclined and ate, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you will hand Me over—one who is eating with Me.”

19They began to be grieved and said to Him one by one, “Surely not I?”

20He said to them, “One of the Twelve, the one dipping with Me into the dish.

21For the Son of Man goes just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would have been good for that man if he had not been born.”

22As they ate, He took bread, pronounced a blessing, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “Take; this is My body.”

23He took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.

24He said to them, “This is My blood of the covenant, poured out for many.

25Truly I tell you, I will certainly no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”

26After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

27Jesus said to them, “You will all stumble, because it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’

28But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”

29Peter said to Him, “Even if all stumble, I will not.”

30Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today, this very night, before a rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.”

31He spoke all the more insistently, “Even if I must die with Thee, I will certainly not deny Thee.” They all said the same.

32They came to a place whose name was Gethsemane. He said to His disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”

33He took Peter, James, and John with Him, and began to be deeply alarmed and distressed.

34He said to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, to the point of death. Remain here and keep watch.”

35Going forward a little, He fell on the ground and prayed that, if possible, the hour might pass from Him.

36He said, “Abba, Father, all things are possible for Thee. Take this cup away from Me. Yet not what I will, but what Thou wilt.”

37He came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Simon, are you sleeping? Could you not keep watch for one hour?

38Keep watch and pray, so that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

39Again He went away and prayed, saying the same word.

40Again He came and found them sleeping, for their eyes were weighed down, and they did not know what to answer Him.

41He came the third time and said to them, “Sleep on now and rest. It is enough. The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.

42Rise; let us go. Look, the one handing Me over has drawn near.”

43Immediately, while He was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.

44The one handing Him over had given them an agreed sign, saying, “The One I kiss is He. Seize Him and lead Him away securely.”

45He came and immediately approached Him, saying, “Rabbi!” Then he kissed Him.

46They laid their hands on Him and seized Him.

47One of those standing nearby drew his sword, struck the high priest’s slave, and cut off his ear.

48Jesus answered them, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as though against a robber?

49Day after day I was with you in the temple, teaching, and you did not seize Me. But this is so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled.”

50They all left Him and fled.

51A certain young man was following Him, wearing a linen cloth over his naked body. They seized him,

52but he left the linen cloth behind and fled naked.

53They led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes assembled.

54Peter followed Him from a distance, as far as inside the high priest’s courtyard. He sat with the attendants and warmed himself at the firelight.

55The chief priests and the whole council sought testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but found none.

56For many bore false witness against Him, but their testimonies did not agree.

57Some stood up and bore false witness against Him, saying,

58“We heard Him say, ‘I will tear down this sanctuary made by hands, and in three days I will build another not made by hands.’”

59Yet even in this their testimony did not agree.

60The high priest stood up in the midst and questioned Jesus, saying, “Dost Thou answer nothing? What is it these men testify against Thee?”

61He remained silent and answered nothing. Again the high priest questioned Him and said to Him, “Art Thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”

62Jesus said, “I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”

63The high priest tore his tunics and said, “What further need have we of witnesses?

64You heard the blasphemy. What is your judgment?” They all condemned Him as deserving death.

65Some began spitting on Him, covering His face, striking Him with their fists, and saying to Him, “Prophesy!” The attendants received Him with slaps.

66While Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the high priest’s female slaves came.

67Seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him and said, “You too were with Jesus the Nazarene.”

68He denied it, saying, “I neither know nor understand what you are saying.” He went outside into the forecourt, and a rooster crowed.

69The female slave saw him and again began saying to those standing nearby, “This man is one of them.”

70Again he denied it. After a little while, those standing nearby again said to Peter, “Truly you are one of them, for you are a Galilean.”

71He began invoking a curse and swearing, “I do not know this Man you are speaking of.”

72Immediately a rooster crowed a second time. Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken to him: “Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” He broke down and wept.

Mark 15

1Immediately in the morning, the chief priests held a consultation with the elders, the scribes, and the whole council. They bound Jesus, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate.

2Pilate questioned Him, “Art Thou the King of the Jews?” He answered him, “You say so.”

3The chief priests accused Him of many things.

4Pilate questioned Him again, saying, “Dost Thou answer nothing? Look how many accusations they bring against Thee.”

5But Jesus gave no further answer, so that Pilate marveled.

6At the feast he used to release for them one prisoner whom they requested.

7The man called Barabbas was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder in the uprising.

8The crowd came up and began asking him to do as he usually did for them.

9Pilate answered them, “Do you want me to release for you the King of the Jews?”

10For he knew that the chief priests had handed Him over out of envy.

11But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas for them instead.

12Pilate answered them again, “Then what do you want me to do with the One you call the King of the Jews?”

13They cried out again, “Crucify Him!”

14Pilate said to them, “Why, what evil has He done?” They cried out all the more, “Crucify Him!”

15Pilate, wanting to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas for them. After having Jesus scourged, he handed Him over to be crucified.

16The soldiers led Him inside the courtyard—that is, the praetorium—and called together the whole cohort.

17They clothed Him in purple and, after weaving a crown of thorns, put it on Him.

18They began saluting Him, “Hail, King of the Jews!”

19They kept striking His head with a reed and spitting on Him, and knelt down to bow before Him.

20After they had mocked Him, they stripped off the purple and put His own garments on Him. They led Him out to crucify Him.

21They compelled a passerby, Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry His cross.

22They brought Him to the place Golgotha, which translated means Place of a Skull.

23They offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.

24They crucified Him and divided His garments, casting a lot over them to determine who would take what.

25It was the third hour when they crucified Him.

26The inscription of the charge against Him was written: “The King of the Jews.”

27They crucified two robbers with Him, one at His right and one at His left.

29Those passing by reviled Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! Thou who dost tear down the sanctuary and build it in three days,

30save Thyself by coming down from the cross!”

31Likewise the chief priests, mocking Him among themselves with the scribes, said, “He saved others; He cannot save Himself.

32Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe.” Those crucified with Him also reproached Him.

33When the sixth hour came, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.

34At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which translated means, “My God, My God, why hast Thou forsaken Me?”

35Some of those standing nearby heard and said, “Look, He is calling Elijah.”

36Someone ran, filled a sponge with sour wine, placed it on a reed, and gave Him a drink, saying, “Leave Him; let us see whether Elijah comes to take Him down.”

37Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.

38The curtain of the sanctuary was torn in two from top to bottom.

39When the centurion standing opposite Him saw that He breathed His last in this way, he said, “Truly this Man was God’s Son.”

40There were also women watching from a distance, among them Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the Little and Joses, and Salome.

41When He was in Galilee, they had followed Him and served Him; there were also many other women who had come up with Him to Jerusalem.

42Evening had already come, and since it was Preparation—that is, the day before the Sabbath—

43Joseph of Arimathea, a respected council member who himself was also awaiting the kingdom of God, came and dared to enter before Pilate and ask for Jesus’ body.

44Pilate marveled that He was already dead. Calling the centurion to him, he asked whether He had died some time ago.

45When he learned from the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.

46Joseph bought a linen cloth, took Him down, wrapped Him in the cloth, and laid Him in a tomb cut out of rock. He rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.

47Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses watched where He was laid.

Mark 16

Textual note: the inherited double brackets mark Mark 16:9–20 as a passage with a distinct textual status. The brackets are retained; a new apparatus review has not been completed.

1When the Sabbath had passed, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so that they might come and anoint Him.

2Very early on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb when the sun had risen.

3They said to one another, “Who will roll the stone away from the entrance of the tomb for us?”

4Looking up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, for it was very large.

5They entered the tomb and saw a young man sitting on the right, clothed in a white robe, and they were greatly alarmed.

6He said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You seek Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has been raised; He is not here. Look, the place where they laid Him.

7But go, tell His disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He told you.’”

8They went out and fled from the tomb, for trembling and astonishment held them. They said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.

9⟦After He had risen early on the first day of the week, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had cast out seven demons.

10She went and reported to those who had been with Him, as they mourned and wept.

11When they heard that He was alive and had been seen by her, they disbelieved.

12After these things, He appeared in another form to two of them as they were walking, going into the country.

13They went away and reported to the rest; they did not believe them either.

14Later He appeared to the Eleven themselves as they reclined at table, and reproached their unbelief and hardness of heart because they had not believed those who had seen Him raised.

15He said to them, “Go into the whole world and proclaim the gospel to all creation.

16The one who believes and is baptized will be saved; the one who disbelieves will be condemned.

17These signs will accompany those who believe: in My name they will cast out demons; they will speak in new tongues;

18and with their hands they will pick up snakes; and if they drink anything deadly, it will certainly not harm them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will be well.”

19So the Lord Jesus, after speaking to them, was taken up into heaven and sat at the right of God.

20They went out and proclaimed everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and confirmed the word through the accompanying signs.⟧
