Acts 9

1Saul, still breathing threat and murder against the Lord’s disciples, went to the high priest

2and asked him for letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any belonging to the Way, both men and women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.

3As he traveled and drew near Damascus, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.

4He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?”

5He said, “Who art Thou, Lord?” He answered, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

6But rise and enter the city, and you will be told what you must do.”

7The men traveling with him stood speechless, hearing the voice but seeing no one.

8Saul rose from the ground, but although his eyes were open, he could see nothing. They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.

9For three days he could not see, and he neither ate nor drank.

10There was a disciple in Damascus named Ananias. The Lord said to him in a vision, “Ananias.” He said, “Here I am, Lord.”

11The Lord said to him, “Rise, go to the street called Straight, and seek in Judas’s house a man named Saul from Tarsus. Look, he is praying,

12and in a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come in and lay hands upon him so that he may regain his sight.”

13Ananias answered, “Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he has done to Thy saints in Jerusalem.

14Here too he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call upon Thy name.”

15But the Lord said to him, “Go, for this man is a chosen vessel for Me, to carry My name before Gentiles and kings and the sons of Israel.

16For I will show him how much he must suffer for My name.”

17Ananias went and entered the house. Laying his hands upon him, he said, “Brother Saul, the Lord has sent me—Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you came—so that you may regain your sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”

18At once something like scales fell from his eyes, and he regained his sight. He rose and was baptized,

19and after taking food he regained strength. He stayed for some days with the disciples in Damascus.

20Immediately he proclaimed Jesus in the synagogues, saying, “He is the Son of God.”

21All who heard him were astonished and said, “Is this not the one who devastated those in Jerusalem who call upon this name? And had he not come here for this purpose, to bring them bound before the chief priests?”

22But Saul grew stronger and confounded the Jews living in Damascus by demonstrating that Jesus is the Christ.

23After many days had passed, the Jews conspired to kill him,

24but their plot became known to Saul. They were also watching the gates day and night to kill him.

25His disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a hamper.

26When he arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they all feared him, not believing that he was a disciple.

27Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles. He related to them how Saul had seen the Lord on the road, how He had spoken to him, and how Saul had spoken boldly in Damascus in the name of Jesus.

28He was with them, going in and out in Jerusalem and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.

29He spoke and disputed with the Hellenists, but they attempted to kill him.

30When the brothers learned this, they brought him down to Caesarea and sent him away to Tarsus.

31So the Church throughout all Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace and was being built up. Walking in the fear of the Lord and in the encouragement of the Holy Spirit, it increased.

32As Peter traveled among them all, he also went down to the saints who lived in Lydda.

33There he found a man named Aeneas who had lain on a mat for eight years, for he was paralyzed.

34Peter said to him, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Rise and make your bed.” At once he rose.

35All who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.

36In Joppa there was a woman disciple named Tabitha, which translated is Dorcas. She was full of good works and acts of charity.

37In those days she became ill and died. They washed her and laid her in an upper room.

38Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, urging, “Do not delay in coming to us.”

39Peter rose and went with them. When he arrived, they brought him into the upper room. All the widows stood beside him weeping and showing the tunics and garments Dorcas had made while she was with them.

40Peter put everyone outside, knelt down, and prayed. Turning toward the body, he said, “Tabitha, rise.” She opened her eyes, saw Peter, and sat up.

41He gave her his hand and raised her up. Then he called the saints and the widows and presented her alive.

42This became known throughout Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.

43He stayed in Joppa for many days with a certain Simon, a tanner.

Acts 10

1In Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion of the cohort called the Italian,

2devout and fearing God with his whole household, giving many alms to the people and praying to God continually.

3About the ninth hour of the day, he clearly saw in a vision an angel of God come in to him and say, “Cornelius.”

4He stared at him in fear and said, “What is it, sir?” The angel said to him, “Your prayers and your alms have ascended as a memorial before God.

5Now send men to Joppa and summon a certain Simon who is called Peter.

6He is staying with a certain Simon, a tanner, whose house is beside the sea.”

7When the angel who spoke to him had gone, Cornelius called two of his household slaves and a devout soldier from among those who attended him.

8He explained everything to them and sent them to Joppa.

9The next day, while they were traveling and approaching the city, Peter went up onto the roof to pray, about the sixth hour.

10He became hungry and wanted to eat. While they were preparing the food, a trance came upon him.

11He saw heaven opened and something like a large sheet descending, being lowered by its four corners to the earth.

12In it were all the four-footed animals and creeping things of the earth and birds of the sky.

13A voice came to him: “Rise, Peter; slaughter and eat.”

14Peter said, “By no means, Lord, for I have never eaten anything common and unclean.”

15A voice came to him again, a second time: “What God has cleansed, you must not call common.”

16This happened three times, and immediately the object was taken up into heaven.

17While Peter was perplexed within himself about what the vision he had seen might mean, look—the men sent by Cornelius, having asked directions to Simon’s house, stood at the gate.

18They called out and asked whether Simon, who was called Peter, was staying there.

19While Peter was pondering the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Look, three men are seeking you.

20Rise, go down, and go with them without hesitation, because I have sent them.”

21Peter went down to the men and said, “I am the one you are seeking. What is the reason you have come?”

22They said, “Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous and God-fearing man well spoken of by the whole Jewish nation, was directed by a holy angel to summon you to his house and hear words from you.”

23So he invited them in and gave them lodging. The next day he rose and went away with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa accompanied him.

24The following day he entered Caesarea. Cornelius was expecting them and had called together his relatives and close friends.

25As Peter was about to enter, Cornelius met him, fell at his feet, and bowed before him.

26But Peter raised him up, saying, “Rise; I too am a human being.”

27While speaking with him, Peter entered and found many people gathered.

28He said to them, “You know how forbidden it is for a Jewish man to associate with or visit someone of another people. Yet God has shown me to call no human being common or unclean.

29Therefore I came without objection when summoned. So I ask, for what reason did you send for me?”

30Cornelius said, “Four days ago, at this hour, I was praying in my house at the ninth hour, and look—a man stood before me in shining clothing.

31He said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your alms have been remembered before God.

32Send, therefore, to Joppa and summon Simon who is called Peter. He is staying in the house of Simon the tanner beside the sea.’

33So I sent to you at once, and you have done well to come. Now we are all here before God to hear everything the Lord has commanded you.”

34Peter opened his mouth and said, “Truly I understand that God shows no partiality,

35but in every nation, whoever fears Him and practices righteousness is acceptable to Him.

36He sent the word to the sons of Israel, proclaiming good news of peace through Jesus Christ—He is Lord of all.

37You know what took place throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee after the baptism John proclaimed:

38Jesus of Nazareth—how God anointed Him with the Holy Spirit and power. He went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with Him.

39We are witnesses of everything He did both in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They also killed Him by hanging Him on a tree.

40God raised Him on the third day and granted that He should appear,

41not to all the people, but to witnesses chosen beforehand by God—to us, who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.

42He commanded us to proclaim to the people and bear solemn witness that He is the One appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead.

43All the prophets bear witness to Him: everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.”

44While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who were hearing the message.

45The believers from the circumcision who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even upon the Gentiles,

46for they heard them speaking in tongues and magnifying God. Then Peter said,

47“Can anyone withhold the water so that these people, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we have, should not be baptized?”

48He ordered them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay for some days.

Acts 11

1The apostles and the brothers throughout Judea heard that the Gentiles too had received the word of God.

2When Peter went up to Jerusalem, those of the circumcision disputed with him,

3saying, “You went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them.”

4Peter began explaining to them in order, saying,

5“I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: something like a large sheet descending, lowered by its four corners from heaven, and it came right to me.

6I looked intently into it and examined it, and I saw the four-footed animals of the earth, wild animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky.

7I also heard a voice saying to me, ‘Rise, Peter; slaughter and eat.’

8But I said, ‘By no means, Lord, for nothing common or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’

9A voice answered a second time from heaven, ‘What God has cleansed, you must not call common.’

10This happened three times, and everything was drawn up again into heaven.

11And look, at once three men stood at the house where we were, sent to me from Caesarea.

12The Spirit told me to go with them, making no distinction. These six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man’s house.

13He reported to us how he had seen the angel standing in his house and saying, ‘Send to Joppa and summon Simon who is called Peter,

14who will speak words to you by which you and your whole household will be saved.’

15As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them just as upon us at the beginning.

16I remembered the Lord’s word, how He said, ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit.’

17If, then, God gave them the same gift as He gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that I could hinder God?”

18When they heard these things, they fell silent and glorified God, saying, “Then God has granted even the Gentiles repentance leading to life.”

19Those who had been scattered by the affliction that arose over Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except Jews alone.

20But some of them were men from Cyprus and Cyrene who came to Antioch and also spoke to the Hellenists, proclaiming the good news of the Lord Jesus.

21The Lord’s hand was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.

22The report about them reached the ears of the Church in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas to travel as far as Antioch.

23When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced and encouraged them all to remain with the Lord with steadfast purpose of heart,

24for he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith. A considerable crowd was added to the Lord.

25He went away to Tarsus to search for Saul,

26and when he found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they gathered with the Church and taught a considerable crowd. It was in Antioch that the disciples were first called Christians.

27In those days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.

28One of them, named Agabus, stood up and indicated through the Spirit that a great famine would come over the whole inhabited world. This happened in the time of Claudius.

29The disciples determined, each according to his means, to send relief to the brothers living in Judea.

30This they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.

Acts 12

1About that time King Herod laid hands on some of the Church to mistreat them.

2He killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.

3When he saw that this pleased the Jews, he proceeded to arrest Peter as well. These were the days of Unleavened Bread.

4He seized him and put him in prison, handing him over to four squads of four soldiers to guard him, intending to bring him out before the people after the Passover.

5So Peter was kept in prison, but earnest prayer for him was being made to God by the Church.

6On the night before Herod was to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, while guards before the door kept watch over the prison.

7And look—an angel of the Lord stood beside him, and light shone in the cell. Striking Peter’s side, he woke him and said, “Rise quickly.” The chains fell from his hands.

8The angel said to him, “Fasten your belt and put on your sandals.” He did so. Then he said to him, “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.”

9Peter went out and followed. He did not know that what was happening through the angel was real; he thought he was seeing a vision.

10They passed the first guard post and the second and came to the iron gate leading into the city. It opened for them of its own accord. They went out and continued along one street, and immediately the angel left him.

11When Peter came to himself, he said, “Now I know truly that the Lord has sent His angel and rescued me from Herod’s hand and from everything the Jewish people were expecting.”

12After considering this, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was called Mark, where many had gathered and were praying.

13When he knocked at the outer gate’s door, a slave girl named Rhoda came to answer.

14Recognizing Peter’s voice, in her joy she did not open the gate, but ran inside and announced that Peter was standing before it.

15They said to her, “You are out of your mind.” But she insisted that it was so. They said, “It is his angel.”

16Peter kept knocking. When they opened the door, they saw him and were astonished.

17He motioned with his hand for them to be silent and related how the Lord had brought him out of prison. He said, “Report these things to James and the brothers.” Then he left and went to another place.

18When day came, there was no small disturbance among the soldiers over what had become of Peter.

19Herod searched for him and did not find him. After examining the guards, he ordered them to be led away for execution. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.

20Herod was fiercely hostile toward the people of Tyre and Sidon. They came to him with one accord and, after winning over Blastus, the king’s chamberlain, asked for peace, because their country received its food from the king’s territory.

21On an appointed day Herod put on royal clothing, sat on the tribunal, and delivered an address to them.

22The populace shouted, “A god’s voice, and not a human being’s!”

23Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him because he did not give the glory to God. He was eaten by worms and breathed his last.

24But the word of God grew and multiplied.

25Barnabas and Saul returned to Jerusalem after completing their service, and took along John who was called Mark.

Acts 13

1In the Church at Antioch there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

2While they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”

3Then, after fasting and praying and laying their hands upon them, they sent them away.

4So, sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia and from there sailed to Cyprus.

5When they came to Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the Jewish synagogues. They also had John as an assistant.

6They traveled through the whole island as far as Paphos and found a certain magician, a Jewish false prophet named Bar-Jesus,

7who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. The proconsul summoned Barnabas and Saul and sought to hear the word of God.

8But Elymas the magician—for that is how his name is translated—opposed them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.

9Saul, who was also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked intently at him

10and said, “You who are full of all deceit and all villainy, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness—will you not stop making crooked the Lord’s straight ways?

11Now look, the Lord’s hand is upon you, and you will be blind, unable to see the sun for a time.” Immediately mist and darkness fell upon him, and he went about seeking people to lead him by the hand.

12When the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, astonished at the teaching of the Lord.

13Paul and his companions sailed from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. John left them and returned to Jerusalem.

14They continued from Perga and arrived at Pisidian Antioch. On the Sabbath day they entered the synagogue and sat down.

15After the reading of the law and the prophets, the synagogue rulers sent word to them, saying, “Men, brothers, if you have a word of encouragement for the people, speak.”

16Paul rose, motioned with his hand, and said, “Men of Israel and you who fear God, listen.

17The God of this people Israel chose our fathers and exalted the people during their stay as strangers in the land of Egypt. With an uplifted arm He led them out of it,

18and for about forty years He put up with their conduct in the wilderness.

19He overthrew seven nations in the land of Canaan and gave their land as an inheritance,

20over about four hundred and fifty years. After these things He gave judges until Samuel the prophet.

21Then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.

22After removing him, He raised up David as king for them, to whom He also bore witness, saying, ‘I have found David son of Jesse, a man after My heart, who will do all My will.’

23From this man’s seed, according to promise, God brought Israel a Savior, Jesus,

24after John had proclaimed, before His coming, a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.

25As John was completing his course, he said, ‘Who do you think I am? I am not that one. But look, One is coming after me, whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.’

26Men, brothers, sons of Abraham’s family, and those among you who fear God: to us the message of this salvation has been sent.

27For those living in Jerusalem and their rulers, failing to recognize Him and the voices of the prophets read every Sabbath, fulfilled those voices by condemning Him.

28Although they found no cause for death, they asked Pilate to have Him killed.

29When they had completed everything written about Him, they took Him down from the tree and laid Him in a tomb.

30But God raised Him from the dead.

31For many days He appeared to those who had gone up with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now His witnesses to the people.

32We proclaim to you the good news of the promise made to the fathers:

33God has fulfilled this for us, their children, by raising up Jesus, as it is also written in the second psalm: ‘Thou art My Son; today I have begotten Thee.’

34God has spoken this way about raising Him from the dead, never again to return to decay: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David.’

35Therefore He also says in another place, ‘Thou wilt not allow Thy Holy One to see decay.’

36For David, after serving his own generation according to God’s purpose, fell asleep, was gathered to his fathers, and saw decay.

37But the One whom God raised did not see decay.

38Therefore let it be known to you, men, brothers, that through Him forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you; and from everything from which you could not be justified in the law of Moses,

39in Him everyone who believes is justified.

40Take care, then, lest what is spoken in the prophets come upon you:

41‘Look, you scoffers, marvel and vanish, for I am doing a work in your days, a work you will never believe even if someone recounts it to you.’”

42As they went out, the people urged that these words be spoken to them on the next Sabbath.

43After the synagogue gathering was dismissed, many Jews and devout converts followed Paul and Barnabas, who spoke with them and urged them to remain in the grace of God.

44On the coming Sabbath, almost the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.

45When the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy and contradicted what Paul was saying, speaking abusively.

46Paul and Barnabas spoke boldly and said, “It was necessary for God’s word to be spoken to you first. Since you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, look—we are turning to the Gentiles.

47For the Lord has commanded us in this way: ‘I have appointed you as a light for Gentiles, so that you may bring salvation to the end of the earth.’”

48When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord, and as many as had been appointed to eternal life believed.

49The word of the Lord spread through the whole region.

50But the Jews stirred up the devout women of high standing and the leading men of the city, raised persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and drove them out of their territory.

51They shook the dust from their feet against them and went to Iconium.

52The disciples were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit.

Acts 14

1In Iconium they entered the Jewish synagogue together and spoke in such a way that a great multitude of both Jews and Greeks believed.

2But the Jews who refused to believe stirred up the Gentiles and embittered their minds against the brothers.

3So they stayed a considerable time, speaking boldly in reliance on the Lord, who bore witness to the word of His grace by granting signs and wonders to take place through their hands.

4The people of the city were divided: some sided with the Jews and others with the apostles.

5When an attempt was made by both Gentiles and Jews, together with their rulers, to mistreat and stone them,

6they learned of it and fled to Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia, and the surrounding region.

7There they continued proclaiming the good news.

8In Lystra a man was sitting who had no strength in his feet, unable to walk from his mother’s womb; he had never walked.

9He listened to Paul speaking. Paul looked intently at him and saw that he had faith to be made well,

10and said with a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet.” He leaped up and began walking.

11When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they raised their voice, saying in Lycaonian, “The gods have come down to us in human likeness.”

12They called Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes, because he was the leading speaker.

13The priest of Zeus, whose shrine was before the city, brought bulls and garlands to the gates and wanted to offer sacrifice with the crowds.

14When the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard this, they tore their garments and rushed out into the crowd, crying out

15and saying, “Men, why are you doing these things? We too are human beings, of the same nature as you. We proclaim good news to you: turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and the sea and everything in them.

16In past generations He allowed all the nations to go their own ways.

17Yet He did not leave Himself without witness in doing good, giving you rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”

18Even by saying these things, they scarcely stopped the crowds from sacrificing to them.

19Jews came from Antioch and Iconium, persuaded the crowds, stoned Paul, and dragged him outside the city, supposing he was dead.

20But when the disciples surrounded him, he rose and entered the city. The next day he went with Barnabas to Derbe.

21After proclaiming the good news to that city and making many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,

22strengthening the souls of the disciples, encouraging them to remain in the faith, and saying, “Through many afflictions we must enter the kingdom of God.”

23They appointed elders for them in each Church and, after praying with fasting, entrusted them to the Lord in whom they had believed.

24They passed through Pisidia and came to Pamphylia.

25After speaking the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

26From there they sailed to Antioch, where they had been entrusted to the grace of God for the work they had now completed.

27When they arrived and gathered the Church, they reported all that God had done with them and how He had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.

28They stayed quite a long time with the disciples.

Acts 15

1Some men came down from Judea and taught the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved.”

2When Paul and Barnabas had a serious disagreement and debate with them, they appointed Paul and Barnabas and some others from among them to go up to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem about this question.

3Sent on their way by the Church, they passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, recounting the conversion of the Gentiles and bringing great joy to all the brothers.

4When they arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the Church, the apostles, and the elders, and reported all that God had done with them.

5But some believers from the party of the Pharisees rose and said, “It is necessary to circumcise them and command them to keep the law of Moses.”

6The apostles and the elders gathered to consider this matter.

7After much debate, Peter rose and said to them, “Men, brothers, you know that in earlier days God made a choice among you, that through my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the good news and believe.

8God, who knows the heart, bore witness to them by giving them the Holy Spirit just as He did to us.

9He made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.

10Now, therefore, why are you testing God by placing upon the disciples’ neck a yoke that neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?

11Rather, we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, in the same way as they are.”

12The whole multitude became silent and listened to Barnabas and Paul relate all the signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.

13After they fell silent, James spoke: “Men, brothers, listen to me.

14Simeon has related how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people for His name.

15With this the words of the prophets agree, as it is written:

16‘After these things I will return and rebuild David’s fallen tent. I will rebuild its ruins and set it upright,

17so that the remnant of humankind and all the nations over whom My name has been called may seek the Lord, says the Lord, who makes these things

18known from long ago.’

19Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those from the Gentiles who are turning to God,

20but should write to them to abstain from the pollutions of idols, sexual immorality, what is strangled, and blood.

21For since ancient times, people in every city have proclaimed Moses, and he is read in the synagogues every Sabbath.”

22Then the apostles and elders, with the whole Church, decided to choose men from among them and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, leading men among the brothers.

23They wrote by their hand: “The apostles and elders, your brothers, to the brothers from the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: greetings.

24Since we have heard that some who went out from among us troubled you with words, unsettling your souls, although we gave them no instruction,

25we have decided with one accord to choose men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,

26men who have given over their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

27We have therefore sent Judas and Silas, who will themselves report the same things by word of mouth.

28For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to place no further burden upon you except these necessary things:

29to abstain from things sacrificed to idols, blood, things strangled, and sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell.”

30After being sent off, they went down to Antioch, gathered the multitude, and delivered the letter.

31When they read it, they rejoiced at its encouragement.

32Judas and Silas, themselves also prophets, encouraged the brothers with many words and strengthened them.

33After spending some time there, they were sent away in peace by the brothers to those who had sent them.

35Paul and Barnabas remained in Antioch, teaching and proclaiming the word of the Lord as good news, along with many others.

36After some days Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us return and visit the brothers in every city where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are.”

37Barnabas wanted to take along John, who was called Mark, as well.

38But Paul considered it right not to take along the man who had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia and had not gone with them to the work.

39A sharp disagreement arose, so that they separated from one another. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus,

40but Paul chose Silas and departed, entrusted by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.

41He traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the Churches.

Acts 16

1He also came to Derbe and Lystra. There was a disciple there named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman, but of a Greek father.

2He was well spoken of by the brothers in Lystra and Iconium.

3Paul wanted him to go with him, and took him and circumcised him because of the Jews in those places, for they all knew that his father was Greek.

4As they traveled through the cities, they handed on to them for observance the decisions made by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem.

5So the Churches were strengthened in the faith and increased in number each day.

6They passed through Phrygia and the Galatian region, having been prevented by the Holy Spirit from speaking the word in Asia.

7When they came near Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus did not permit them.

8Passing by Mysia, they went down to Troas.

9During the night a vision appeared to Paul: a Macedonian man was standing and urging him, saying, “Cross over to Macedonia and help us.”

10When he had seen the vision, we immediately sought to go out to Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to proclaim the good news to them.

11We sailed from Troas and made a straight course to Samothrace, and on the next day to Neapolis,

12and from there to Philippi, a city of the first district of Macedonia and a colony. We stayed in that city for some days.

13On the Sabbath day we went outside the gate beside a river, where we thought there was a place of prayer. We sat down and spoke to the women who had gathered.

14A woman named Lydia, a seller of purple goods from the city of Thyatira, who worshiped God, was listening. The Lord opened her heart to attend to what Paul was saying.

15After she and her household were baptized, she urged us, saying, “If you have judged me faithful to the Lord, come into my house and stay.” And she prevailed upon us.

16As we were going to the place of prayer, a slave girl with a spirit of divination met us. She brought her masters much profit by fortune-telling.

17She followed Paul and us, crying out, “These men are servants of God Most High, who proclaim to you the way of salvation.”

18She kept doing this for many days. Paul, greatly troubled, turned and said to the spirit, “I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her.” It came out that very hour.

19When her masters saw that their hope of profit had gone out, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers.

20They brought them before the magistrates and said, “These men are throwing our city into turmoil. They are Jews,

21and they proclaim customs that we, being Romans, are not permitted to accept or practice.”

22The crowd joined the attack against them. The magistrates tore off their garments and ordered them to be beaten with rods.

23After inflicting many blows on them, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to keep them securely.

24Having received such an order, he put them in the inner prison and secured their feet in the stocks.

25About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, while the prisoners listened to them.

26Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the jail’s foundations were shaken. At once all the doors opened, and everyone’s bonds were loosened.

27The jailer awoke and saw the prison doors open. He drew his sword and was about to kill himself, supposing the prisoners had escaped.

28But Paul cried with a loud voice, “Do yourself no harm, for we are all here.”

29He called for lights, rushed inside, and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.

30He brought them outside and said, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”

31They said, “Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household.”

32They spoke the word of the Lord to him, together with all who were in his house.

33At that very hour of the night he took them and washed their wounds. Immediately he and all his people were baptized.

34He brought them up into his house, set food before them, and rejoiced with his whole household, having believed in God.

35When day came, the magistrates sent the officers, saying, “Release those men.”

36The jailer reported these words to Paul: “The magistrates have sent word for you to be released. Now come out and go in peace.”

37But Paul said to them, “They beat us publicly without a verdict, although we are Roman citizens, and threw us into prison. And now are they sending us away secretly? No indeed! Let them come themselves and lead us out.”

38The officers reported these words to the magistrates, and they were afraid when they heard that the men were Romans.

39They came and appealed to them, led them out, and asked them to leave the city.

40After leaving the prison, they went to Lydia’s house. They saw the brothers, encouraged them, and departed.

Acts 17

1After traveling through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

2As was his custom, Paul went in to them, and for three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,

3explaining and setting before them that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead, and saying, “This Jesus whom I proclaim to you is the Christ.”

4Some of them were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, as did a great multitude of devout Greeks and not a few of the leading women.

5But the Jews became jealous and took some wicked men from the marketplace, gathered a mob, and threw the city into turmoil. They attacked Jason’s house and sought to bring Paul and Silas out to the populace.

6When they did not find them, they dragged Jason and some brothers before the city officials, shouting, “These men who have upset the inhabited world have come here too,

7and Jason has welcomed them. They all act against Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, Jesus.”

8They disturbed the crowd and the city officials who heard these things.

9After taking security from Jason and the others, the officials released them.

10The brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Berea. When they arrived, they went into the Jewish synagogue.

11These people were more noble-minded than those in Thessalonica: they welcomed the word with all eagerness, examining the Scriptures daily to see whether these things were so.

12Many of them therefore believed, as did not a few Greek women of high standing and men.

13But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that the word of God had also been proclaimed by Paul in Berea, they came there too, stirring up and disturbing the crowds.

14Then the brothers immediately sent Paul away to go as far as the sea, while Silas and Timothy remained there.

15Those escorting Paul brought him as far as Athens. After receiving an order for Silas and Timothy to come to him as quickly as possible, they departed.

16While Paul waited for them in Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he observed that the city was full of idols.

17So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the worshipers, and in the marketplace every day with those who happened to be there.

18Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also engaged him. Some said, “What is this babbler trying to say?” Others said, “He seems to be a proclaimer of foreign divinities,” because he proclaimed the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.

19They took him and brought him to the Areopagus, saying, “May we know what this new teaching is that you are speaking?

20For you are bringing some strange things to our ears. We therefore wish to know what these things mean.”

21Now all the Athenians and the foreigners staying there spent their free time doing nothing but telling or hearing the latest thing.

22Paul stood in the midst of the Areopagus and said, “Men of Athens, I perceive that in every respect you are very religious.

23For as I passed through and observed your objects of worship, I also found an altar inscribed, ‘To an unknown god.’ What you worship without knowing, this I proclaim to you.

24The God who made the world and everything in it, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in sanctuaries made by hands.

25Nor is He served by human hands as though He needed anything, since He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything.

26From one He made every nation of humanity to live upon the whole face of the earth, determining their appointed times and the boundaries of their dwelling,

27so that they might seek God, if perhaps they might feel their way toward Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.

28For in Him we live and move and exist, as even some of your own poets have said, ‘For we too are His offspring.’

29Since we are God’s offspring, we ought not to think that the divine nature is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by human art and thought.

30Therefore, having overlooked the times of ignorance, God now commands all people everywhere to repent,

31because He has fixed a day on which He will judge the inhabited world in righteousness through a Man whom He appointed, giving assurance to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”

32When they heard of a resurrection of the dead, some mocked, while others said, “We will hear you again about this.”

33So Paul went out from their midst.

34But some people joined him and believed, among them Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others with them.

Acts 18

1After these things he left Athens and came to Corinth.

2He found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to them,

3and because he practiced the same trade, he stayed with them and worked, for they were tentmakers by trade.

4Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue and sought to persuade both Jews and Greeks.

5When Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself to the word, bearing solemn witness to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.

6When they opposed him and spoke abusively, he shook out his garments and said to them, “Your blood be upon your own heads. I am clean. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”

7He left there and entered the house of a man named Titius Justus, a worshiper of God, whose house was next to the synagogue.

8Crispus, the synagogue ruler, believed in the Lord with his whole household. Many of the Corinthians who heard believed and were baptized.

9The Lord said to Paul by a vision in the night, “Do not fear, but speak and do not be silent,

10because I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, for I have many people in this city.”

11He stayed a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.

12While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews rose together against Paul and brought him before the tribunal,

13saying, “This man persuades people to worship God contrary to the law.”

14As Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If it were some wrongdoing or wicked crime, O Jews, I would have reason to hear you out.

15But if these are questions about a word, names, and your own law, see to it yourselves. I do not wish to be a judge of these things.”

16He drove them away from the tribunal.

17They all seized Sosthenes, the synagogue ruler, and beat him before the tribunal. Gallio cared about none of these things.

18Paul stayed many more days, then took leave of the brothers and sailed for Syria, with Priscilla and Aquila. He had cut his hair at Cenchreae, for he had a vow.

19They arrived at Ephesus, and he left them there. He himself entered the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.

20When they asked him to stay for a longer time, he did not agree.

21Instead, he took leave of them, saying, “I will return to you again, God willing,” and sailed from Ephesus.

22He landed at Caesarea, went up and greeted the Church, and went down to Antioch.

23After spending some time there, he departed and traveled from place to place through the Galatian region and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.

24A Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, powerful in the Scriptures.

25He had been instructed in the way of the Lord, and being fervent in spirit, he spoke and taught accurately the things concerning Jesus, though he knew only John’s baptism.

26He began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained the way of God to him more accurately.

27When he wished to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples to welcome him. On arriving, he greatly helped those who had believed through grace,

28for he vigorously refuted the Jews in public, demonstrating through the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.

Acts 19

1While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul passed through the upper regions and came down to Ephesus. He found some disciples

2and said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” They said to him, “We have not even heard whether there is a Holy Spirit.”

3He said, “Into what, then, were you baptized?” They said, “Into John’s baptism.”

4Paul said, “John baptized with a baptism of repentance, telling the people to believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Jesus.”

5When they heard this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.

6When Paul laid his hands upon them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.

7There were about twelve men in all.

8He entered the synagogue and spoke boldly for three months, reasoning and persuading concerning the kingdom of God.

9But when some became hardened and refused to believe, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he withdrew from them and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.

10This continued for two years, so that all who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks.

11God was doing extraordinary mighty works through Paul’s hands,

12so that even cloths or aprons from contact with his skin were carried to the sick, and their diseases left them and the evil spirits went out.

13Some itinerant Jewish exorcists also attempted to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those who had evil spirits, saying, “I solemnly charge you by the Jesus whom Paul proclaims.”

14Seven sons of a certain Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.

15But the evil spirit answered them, “Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize, but who are you?”

16The man in whom the evil spirit was leaped upon them, mastered both of them, and overpowered them, so that they fled from that house naked and wounded.

17This became known to all the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus. Fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.

18Many who had believed came, confessing and reporting their practices.

19A considerable number who had practiced magic brought their books together and burned them before everyone. They calculated their prices and found the total to be fifty thousand in silver.

20In this way the word of the Lord grew mightily and prevailed.

21After these things were completed, Paul resolved in spirit to pass through Macedonia and Achaia and go to Jerusalem, saying, “After I have been there, I must also see Rome.”

22He sent two of those who assisted him, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he himself remained in Asia for a time.

23About that time a serious disturbance arose concerning the Way.

24A silversmith named Demetrius, who made silver shrines of Artemis, provided considerable business for the craftsmen.

25He gathered them and the workers in related trades and said, “Men, you know that our prosperity comes from this business.

26You see and hear that not only in Ephesus but in almost all Asia this Paul has persuaded and turned away a considerable crowd, saying that things made by hands are not gods.

27There is danger not only that this trade of ours will fall into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be reckoned as nothing, and that she whom all Asia and the inhabited world worship will be stripped of her magnificence.”

28When they heard this, they became full of rage and cried out, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

29The city was filled with confusion. They rushed together into the theater, seizing Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians who traveled with Paul.

30Paul wanted to enter among the populace, but the disciples would not let him.

31Even some of the Asiarchs, who were his friends, sent to him and urged him not to venture into the theater.

32Some shouted one thing and some another, for the assembly was confused, and most did not know why they had come together.

33They prompted Alexander from the crowd, the Jews having put him forward. Alexander motioned with his hand and wished to make a defense before the populace.

34When they recognized that he was a Jew, one cry arose from them all for about two hours: “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

35The city secretary quieted the crowd and said, “Men of Ephesus, who among human beings does not know that the city of the Ephesians is temple-keeper of the great Artemis and of what fell from Zeus?

36Since these things are undeniable, you must remain calm and do nothing rash.

37For you have brought these men here, though they are neither temple-robbers nor blasphemers of our goddess.

38If Demetrius and the craftsmen with him have a charge against anyone, court sessions are held and proconsuls are available; let them bring charges against one another.

39But if you seek anything further, it will be settled in the lawful assembly.

40aFor we are in danger of being charged with rioting over today’s events, since there is no cause for it; we will not be able to give an account of this gathering.”

40bAfter saying these things, he dismissed the assembly.

Acts 20

1After the uproar ceased, Paul summoned the disciples and encouraged them. Taking leave of them, he departed for Macedonia.

2He passed through those regions and encouraged them with many words, then came to Greece

3and spent three months there. When a plot was made against him by the Jews as he was about to sail for Syria, he decided to return through Macedonia.

4He was accompanied by Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea; Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica; Gaius from Derbe, and Timothy; and Tychicus and Trophimus from Asia.

5These men went ahead and waited for us in Troas.

6We sailed from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread and came to them at Troas in five days, where we stayed seven days.

7On the first day of the week, when we had gathered to break bread, Paul spoke with them. He intended to leave the next day and prolonged his message until midnight.

8There were many lamps in the upper room where we had gathered.

9A young man named Eutychus sat in the window and was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul continued speaking at length. Overcome by sleep, he fell down from the third story and was picked up dead.

10Paul went down, fell upon him, embraced him, and said, “Do not be alarmed, for his life is in him.”

11He went back up, broke the bread and ate, and talked for a long time until dawn. Then he departed.

12They brought the boy away alive and were greatly comforted.

13We went ahead to the ship and sailed for Assos, intending to take Paul aboard there, for he had arranged it this way, intending himself to travel on foot.

14When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and came to Mitylene.

15Sailing from there, the next day we arrived opposite Chios; on the following day we put in at Samos, and on the next we came to Miletus.

16For Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus so that he would not spend time in Asia. He was hurrying, if possible, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.

17From Miletus he sent to Ephesus and summoned the elders of the Church.

18When they came to him, he said, “You know how I was with you the whole time, from the first day I set foot in Asia,

19serving the Lord with all humility, tears, and trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews.

20I did not hold back from declaring anything beneficial to you and teaching you publicly and from house to house,

21bearing solemn witness to both Jews and Greeks of repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus.

22And now, look, bound in spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will meet me there,

23except that in every city the Holy Spirit bears witness to me, saying that bonds and afflictions await me.

24But I consider my life of no value to myself, so that I may complete my course and the ministry I received from the Lord Jesus: to bear solemn witness to the good news of God’s grace.

25And now, look, I know that none of you among whom I went about proclaiming the kingdom will see my face again.

26Therefore I testify to you this very day that I am clean from the blood of all,

27for I did not hold back from declaring to you the whole purpose of God.

28Pay attention to yourselves and to all the flock, among whom the Holy Spirit has placed you as overseers, to shepherd the Church of God, which He acquired through His own blood.

29I know that after my departure fierce wolves will enter among you, not sparing the flock.

30Even from among you yourselves men will arise, speaking distorted things to draw the disciples away after themselves.

31Therefore stay awake, remembering that for three years, night and day, I never ceased admonishing each one with tears.

32And now I entrust you to God and to the word of His grace, which is able to build you up and give you the inheritance among all who have been sanctified.

33I coveted no one’s silver or gold or clothing.

34You yourselves know that these hands served my needs and those of the people with me.

35In everything I showed you that by working in this way we must support the weak and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that He Himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”

36After saying these things, he knelt down with them all and prayed.

37They all wept greatly, threw their arms around Paul’s neck, and kissed him repeatedly,

38grieving most of all over the word he had spoken, that they would no longer see his face. They accompanied him to the ship.

Acts 21

1When we had torn ourselves away from them and set sail, we made a straight course to Cos, the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

2We found a ship crossing to Phoenicia, went aboard, and set sail.

3We sighted Cyprus and passed it on our left, sailed toward Syria, and landed at Tyre, for the ship was to unload its cargo there.

4We sought out the disciples and stayed there seven days. Through the Spirit they told Paul not to set foot in Jerusalem.

5When our days there were completed, we left and went on our way. They all accompanied us, with wives and children, as far as outside the city. We knelt on the beach and prayed,

6then said farewell to one another. We boarded the ship, and they returned to their homes.

7Completing the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais, greeted the brothers, and stayed with them for one day.

8The next day we departed and came to Caesarea. We entered the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.

9He had four daughters who were virgins and prophesied.

10While we stayed for several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

11He came to us, took Paul’s belt, bound his own feet and hands, and said, “Thus says the Holy Spirit: ‘The Jews in Jerusalem will bind the man whose belt this is in this way and hand him over into Gentile hands.’”

12When we heard these things, both we and the local people urged him not to go up to Jerusalem.

13Then Paul answered, “What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”

14Since he would not be persuaded, we became silent and said, “Let the Lord’s will be done.”

15After these days we made our preparations and went up to Jerusalem.

16Some disciples from Caesarea also went with us, taking us to a certain Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we were to lodge.

17When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us gladly.

18The next day Paul went with us to James, and all the elders were present.

19After greeting them, he related one by one the things God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.

20When they heard, they glorified God and said to him, “You see, brother, how many tens of thousands of Jews have believed, and they are all zealous for the law.

21They have been informed about you that you teach all the Jews among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or walk in the customs.

22What, then, is to be done? They will certainly hear that you have come.

23Therefore do what we tell you. We have four men who have taken a vow upon themselves.

24Take these men, purify yourself with them, and pay their expenses so that they may shave their heads. Then everyone will know that there is nothing to what they have been told about you, but that you yourself also walk in step, keeping the law.

25But concerning the Gentiles who have believed, we have sent word, judging that they should keep themselves from what is sacrificed to idols, blood, what is strangled, and sexual immorality.”

26Then Paul took the men, and on the next day, after purifying himself with them, he entered the temple, giving notice of the completion of the days of purification, up to the presentation of the offering for each one of them.

27When the seven days were about to be completed, the Jews from Asia saw him in the temple, stirred up the whole crowd, and laid hands on him,

28crying, “Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against the people, the law, and this place. Moreover, he has even brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.”

29For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city and supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.

30The whole city was stirred, and the people ran together. They seized Paul and dragged him outside the temple, and immediately the doors were shut.

31While they were seeking to kill him, a report reached the tribune of the cohort that all Jerusalem was in confusion.

32He immediately took soldiers and centurions and ran down to them. When they saw the tribune and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.

33Then the tribune approached, seized him, and ordered him bound with two chains. He asked who he was and what he had done.

34Some in the crowd shouted one thing and some another. Since he could learn nothing certain because of the uproar, he ordered Paul to be brought into the barracks.

35When he reached the steps, the soldiers had to carry him because of the crowd’s violence,

36for the multitude of the people followed, crying, “Away with him!”

37As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he said to the tribune, “May I say something to you?” He said, “Do you know Greek?

38Then are you not the Egyptian who some time ago stirred up a revolt and led the four thousand men of the Sicarii into the wilderness?”

39Paul said, “I am a Jewish man from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. I ask you, allow me to speak to the people.”

40When he gave permission, Paul stood on the steps and motioned with his hand to the people. When a great silence fell, he addressed them in the Hebrew language, saying:

Acts 22

1“Men, brothers and fathers, hear the defense I now make before you.”

2When they heard that he addressed them in the Hebrew language, they became still quieter. He said:

3“I am a Jewish man, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, educated in the strict observance of the ancestral law, zealous for God as all of you are today.

4I persecuted this Way to the point of death, binding and handing over to prisons both men and women,

5as the high priest and the whole council of elders can testify for me. From them I also received letters to the brothers, and I went toward Damascus to bring those there bound to Jerusalem for punishment.

6As I was traveling and drawing near Damascus, about noon, a brilliant light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.

7I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?’

8I answered, ‘Who art Thou, Lord?’ He said to me, ‘I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you are persecuting.’

9Those with me saw the light, but they did not hear the voice of the One speaking to me.

10I said, ‘What should I do, Lord?’ The Lord said to me, ‘Rise and go into Damascus, and there you will be told about everything appointed for you to do.’

11Since I could not see because of the brightness of that light, I was led by the hand by those with me and came into Damascus.

12A certain Ananias, a man devout according to the law and well spoken of by all the Jews living there,

13came to me, stood beside me, and said, ‘Brother Saul, regain your sight.’ At that very hour I regained my sight and looked at him.

14He said, ‘The God of our fathers appointed you to know His will, to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from His mouth,

15for you will be His witness to all people of what you have seen and heard.

16Now why do you delay? Rise, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling upon His name.’

17After I returned to Jerusalem, while I was praying in the temple, I fell into a trance

18and saw Him saying to me, ‘Hurry, and go out quickly from Jerusalem, because they will not accept your testimony about Me.’

19I said, ‘Lord, they themselves know that I used to imprison and beat in the synagogues those who believe in Thee.

20And when the blood of Stephen, Thy witness, was being poured out, I myself stood by, approving and guarding the garments of those who were killing him.’

21He said to me, ‘Go, for I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’”

22They listened to him until this statement, then raised their voice and said, “Remove such a man from the earth, for he ought not to live.”

23As they shouted, flung their garments, and threw dust into the air,

24the tribune ordered him brought into the barracks and directed that he be examined by scourging, so that he might learn why they were shouting against him in this way.

25As they stretched him out with the straps, Paul said to the centurion standing nearby, “Is it lawful for you to scourge a Roman citizen who has not been condemned?”

26When the centurion heard this, he went to the tribune and reported it, saying, “What are you about to do? This man is a Roman.”

27The tribune came and said to him, “Tell me, are you a Roman?” He said, “Yes.”

28The tribune answered, “I acquired this citizenship for a large sum.” Paul said, “But I was born with it.”

29Those about to examine him immediately withdrew. The tribune too was afraid when he learned that Paul was a Roman and that he had bound him.

30The next day, wishing to learn with certainty what accusation the Jews were bringing against him, he unbound him and ordered the chief priests and the whole council to assemble. He brought Paul down and set him before them.

Acts 23

1Paul looked intently at the council and said, “Men, brothers, I have conducted my life before God with an entirely good conscience to this day.”

2The high priest Ananias ordered those standing beside him to strike his mouth.

3Then Paul said to him, “God is going to strike you, whitewashed wall! You sit judging me according to the law, yet in violation of the law you order me struck?”

4Those standing nearby said, “Are you insulting God’s high priest?”

5Paul said, “Brothers, I did not know that he was high priest, for it is written, ‘You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.’”

6When Paul perceived that one part consisted of Sadducees and the other of Pharisees, he cried out in the council, “Men, brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. I am being judged concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead.”

7As he said this, dissension arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the multitude was divided.

8For the Sadducees say there is no resurrection, nor angel nor spirit, but the Pharisees acknowledge both.

9A great outcry arose, and some scribes of the Pharisees’ party stood up and argued fiercely, saying, “We find nothing wrong in this man. But what if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?”

10As the dispute intensified, the tribune feared Paul would be torn apart by them. He ordered the troops to go down, snatch him from their midst, and bring him into the barracks.

11The following night the Lord stood beside him and said, “Take courage, for as you have borne solemn witness about Me in Jerusalem, so you must also testify in Rome.”

12When day came, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves under a curse, saying they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.

13More than forty had made this conspiracy.

14They went to the chief priests and elders and said, “We have bound ourselves under a solemn curse to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.

15Now, therefore, you and the council should inform the tribune to bring him down to you, as though you intended to determine his case more accurately. We are ready to kill him before he comes near.”

16Paul’s sister’s son heard about the ambush, came and entered the barracks, and reported it to Paul.

17Paul called one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the tribune, for he has something to report to him.”

18So he took him and brought him to the tribune, saying, “The prisoner Paul called me and asked me to bring this young man to you, since he has something to tell you.”

19The tribune took him by the hand, withdrew privately, and asked, “What is it that you have to report to me?”

20He said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though it intended to inquire more accurately about him.

21But do not be persuaded by them, for more than forty men among them are lying in wait for him. They have bound themselves under a curse neither to eat nor to drink until they kill him, and now they are ready, awaiting your agreement.”

22The tribune dismissed the young man, ordering him, “Tell no one that you have disclosed these things to me.”

23He called two of the centurions and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, with seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen, leaving at the third hour of the night.”

24He also ordered mounts to be provided so that they could put Paul on them and bring him safely to Felix the governor.

25He wrote a letter in this form:

26“Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix: greetings.

27This man was seized by the Jews and was about to be killed by them when I came with the troops and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.

28Wishing to learn the reason they accused him, I brought him down to their council.

29I found him accused over questions of their law, but under no charge deserving death or imprisonment.

30When a plot against the man was disclosed to me, I immediately sent him to you, also ordering his accusers to state their case against him before you.”

31So the soldiers, according to their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.

32The next day they left the horsemen to go on with him and returned to the barracks.

33When the horsemen entered Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and also presented Paul before him.

34He read it, asked what province Paul was from, and learned that he was from Cilicia.

35He said, “I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive,” and ordered him kept under guard in Herod’s praetorium.

Acts 24

1After five days the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and an advocate named Tertullus. They presented their case against Paul to the governor.

2When Paul was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, “Through you we enjoy much peace, and reforms are being made for this nation through your foresight.

3In every way and everywhere we acknowledge this, most excellent Felix, with all gratitude.

4But so that I may not detain you further, I ask you in your kindness to hear us briefly.

5For we have found this man to be a plague, stirring up disturbances among all the Jews throughout the inhabited world, and a ringleader of the party of the Nazarenes.

6He even tried to profane the temple, and we seized him.

8By examining him yourself, you will be able to learn about all these things of which we accuse him.”

9The Jews also joined in the attack, asserting that these things were so.

10When the governor motioned for him to speak, Paul answered, “Knowing that you have been a judge of this nation for many years, I cheerfully make my defense concerning myself.

11You can confirm that it is no more than twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem to worship.

12They did not find me disputing with anyone or gathering a crowd, whether in the temple, in the synagogues, or in the city.

13Nor can they present proof to you of the things they now accuse me of.

14But I confess this to you: according to the Way, which they call a sect, I worship the God of our fathers, believing everything in accordance with the law and everything written in the prophets,

15having hope in God—which these people themselves also await—that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.

16For this reason I myself strive always to have a blameless conscience toward God and human beings.

17After several years I came to bring alms to my nation and offerings.

18While I was engaged in these, they found me purified in the temple, with neither a crowd nor an uproar.

19But there were some Jews from Asia who ought to be present before you and bring charges, if they had anything against me.

20Or let these men themselves say what wrongdoing they found when I stood before the council,

21except for this one declaration I cried out while standing among them: ‘It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am being judged before you today.’”

22Felix, who had more accurate knowledge of the Way, adjourned their case, saying, “When Lysias the tribune comes down, I will decide your case.”

23He ordered the centurion to keep Paul in custody but grant him some freedom, and not prevent any of his own people from attending to him.

24After some days Felix came with his own wife Drusilla, who was Jewish. He summoned Paul and heard him concerning faith in Christ Jesus.

25As Paul reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix became afraid and answered, “Go away for now. When I find an opportunity, I will summon you.”

26At the same time he hoped that Paul would give him money. Therefore he summoned him more frequently and conversed with him.

27When two years were completed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. Wishing to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul bound.

Acts 25

1Three days after arriving in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.

2The chief priests and the leading men of the Jews presented their case against Paul to him and urged him,

3asking as a favor against Paul that he summon him to Jerusalem, while planning an ambush to kill him along the road.

4Festus answered that Paul was being kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would soon be going there.

5He said, “Let the influential men among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him.”

6After staying among them no more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea. The next day he sat on the tribunal and ordered Paul to be brought in.

7When he arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many serious accusations that they could not prove.

8Paul made his defense: “I have committed no offense against the law of the Jews, against the temple, or against Caesar.”

9But Festus, wishing to gain favor with the Jews, answered Paul, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and be judged there before me concerning these things?”

10Paul said, “I am standing before Caesar’s tribunal, where I ought to be judged. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.

11If, then, I am doing wrong and have done anything deserving death, I do not refuse to die. But if there is nothing to their accusations against me, no one can hand me over to them as a favor. I appeal to Caesar.”

12Then Festus conferred with his council and answered, “You have appealed to Caesar; to Caesar you will go.”

13After some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived in Caesarea to greet Festus.

14While they stayed there for several days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying, “There is a man left as a prisoner by Felix.

15When I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders of the Jews presented their case against him, asking for his condemnation.

16I answered them that it is not Roman custom to hand anyone over as a favor before the accused has met his accusers face to face and received an opportunity to defend himself concerning the charge.

17So when they gathered here, I made no delay, but on the next day sat on the tribunal and ordered the man brought in.

18When his accusers stood up, they brought no charge of the evil things I had expected.

19Instead, they had certain disputes with him concerning their own religion and a certain Jesus who had died, whom Paul asserted to be alive.

20Uncertain how to investigate these matters, I asked whether he wished to go to Jerusalem and be judged there concerning them.

21But when Paul appealed to be kept for Augustus’s decision, I ordered him held until I could send him to Caesar.”

22Agrippa said to Festus, “I would like to hear the man myself.” He said, “Tomorrow you will hear him.”

23The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the audience hall with the tribunes and the city’s prominent men. At Festus’s order, Paul was brought in.

24Festus said, “King Agrippa and all you men present with us, you see this man concerning whom the whole multitude of the Jews petitioned me, both in Jerusalem and here, shouting that he ought not to live any longer.

25I found that he had done nothing deserving death, but since he himself appealed to Augustus, I decided to send him.

26I have nothing certain to write to the sovereign about him. Therefore I have brought him before you all, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after the examination I may have something to write.

27For it seems unreasonable to me to send a prisoner without also indicating the charges against him.”

Acts 26

1Agrippa said to Paul, “You are permitted to speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand and made his defense:

2“Concerning everything of which I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to make my defense before you today,

3especially since you are familiar with all the Jewish customs and disputes. Therefore I ask you to hear me patiently.

4All the Jews know my manner of life from my youth, lived from the beginning among my nation and in Jerusalem.

5They have known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that I lived as a Pharisee according to the strictest party of our religion.

6Now I stand on trial because of hope in the promise made by God to our fathers,

7which our twelve tribes, earnestly worshiping night and day, hope to attain. It is concerning this hope that I am accused by Jews, O king.

8Why do you consider it unbelievable that God raises the dead?

9I myself thought that I must do many things against the name of Jesus the Nazarene.

10This I did in Jerusalem: I shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests, and when they were being killed, I cast my vote against them.

11I punished them often in all the synagogues and tried to compel them to blaspheme. In my intense rage against them, I pursued them even to foreign cities.

12In this pursuit I was traveling to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,

13when at midday, O king, I saw along the road a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those traveling with me.

14When we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me in the Hebrew language: ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me? It is hard for you to kick against goads.’

15I said, ‘Who art Thou, Lord?’ The Lord said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

16But rise and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you a servant and witness of the things in which you have seen Me and those in which I will appear to you,

17rescuing you from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I am sending you,

18to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from Satan’s authority to God, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an allotted share among those sanctified by faith in Me.’

19Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,

20but proclaimed first to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, throughout all the country of Judea, and to the Gentiles that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.

21For these reasons the Jews seized me in the temple and tried to kill me.

22Having therefore received help from God, I stand to this day, testifying to small and great, saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen:

23that the Christ would suffer and, as the first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light both to the people and to the Gentiles.”

24As he was making this defense, Festus said with a loud voice, “You are mad, Paul! Your great learning is turning you to madness.”

25Paul said, “I am not mad, most excellent Festus, but I speak words of truth and sound judgment.

26For the king knows about these things, and I speak freely to him. I am persuaded that none of these things has escaped his notice, for this has not been done in a corner.

27King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.”

28Agrippa said to Paul, “With so little, you are trying to persuade me to become a Christian.”

29Paul said, “Whether with little or with much, I would pray to God that not only you but also all who hear me today might become as I am, except for these bonds.”

30The king rose, along with the governor, Bernice, and those seated with them.

31After withdrawing, they spoke to one another, saying, “This man is doing nothing deserving death or imprisonment.”

32Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
