Acts 27

1When it was decided that we should sail to Italy, they handed Paul and some other prisoners over to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan cohort.

2We boarded a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to the ports along Asia, and set sail. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.

3The next day we put in at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and allowed him to go to his friends and receive care.

4From there we set sail and sailed under the shelter of Cyprus because the winds were contrary.

5We crossed the open sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia and came to Myra in Lycia.

6There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing to Italy and put us aboard it.

7We sailed slowly for many days and with difficulty came off Cnidus. Since the wind would not permit us to proceed, we sailed under the shelter of Crete off Salmone.

8Coasting along it with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near which was the city of Lasea.

9Much time had passed, and sailing was already dangerous because even the Fast had now gone by. Paul advised them,

10saying, “Men, I perceive that the voyage will bring damage and great loss, not only of the cargo and the ship but also of our lives.”

11But the centurion was more persuaded by the pilot and the shipowner than by what Paul said.

12Since the harbor was unsuitable for wintering, the majority decided to sail from there, hoping somehow to reach Phoenix, a harbor of Crete facing southwest and northwest, and winter there.

13When a south wind blew gently, they supposed they had gained their purpose, weighed anchor, and sailed close along Crete.

14But not long afterward a hurricane wind called Euraquilo rushed down from the island.

15The ship was seized and could not face the wind, so we gave way and were driven along.

16Running under the shelter of a small island called Cauda, we were barely able to secure the boat.

17After hoisting it aboard, they used supports to hold the ship together from beneath. Fearing they would run aground on the Syrtis, they lowered the gear and were driven along in this way.

18As we were violently battered by the storm, the next day they began throwing cargo overboard.

19On the third day they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.

20When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and a fierce storm kept battering us, all remaining hope of our being saved was taken away.

21After a long time without food, Paul stood among them and said, “Men, you ought to have listened to me and not sailed from Crete, and so avoided this damage and loss.

22Now I urge you to take courage, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

23For this night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I worship stood beside me,

24saying, ‘Do not fear, Paul. You must stand before Caesar, and look, God has granted you all who sail with you.’

25Therefore take courage, men, for I believe God that it will be just as I have been told.

26But we must run aground on some island.”

27When the fourteenth night came, as we were being driven across the Adria, about midnight the sailors suspected that some land was approaching them.

28They took a sounding and found twenty fathoms. After going a little farther, they sounded again and found fifteen fathoms.

29Fearing we might run aground somewhere on rocky places, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for day to come.

30The sailors sought to flee from the ship and lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they were about to lay out anchors from the bow.

31Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain in the ship, you cannot be saved.”

32Then the soldiers cut the boat’s ropes and let it fall away.

33As day was about to come, Paul urged everyone to take food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day you have continued waiting without food, taking nothing.

34Therefore I urge you to take food, for this is for your safety. Not a hair from the head of any of you will be lost.”

35After saying these things, he took bread, gave thanks to God before everyone, broke it, and began to eat.

36They all took courage and themselves took food.

37There were two hundred and seventy-six persons in all aboard the ship.

38When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.

39When day came, they did not recognize the land, but noticed a bay with a beach and planned, if they could, to drive the ship onto it.

40They cast off the anchors and left them in the sea, while also loosening the lashings of the steering oars. They raised the foresail to the wind and headed for the beach.

41But they struck a place between two seas and ran the ship aground. The bow stuck fast and remained immovable, while the stern was breaking apart under the force of the waves.

42The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so that none might swim away and escape.

43But the centurion, wishing to save Paul, prevented them from carrying out their plan. He ordered those able to swim to jump overboard first and make for land,

44and the rest to follow, some on planks and some on pieces from the ship. In this way everyone reached land safely.

Acts 28

1After reaching safety, we learned that the island was called Melite.

2The people who did not speak Greek showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed us all because of the rain that had begun and because of the cold.

3Paul gathered a bundle of brushwood and put it on the fire. A viper came out because of the heat and fastened onto his hand.

4When the people who did not speak Greek saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “This man is certainly a murderer. Although he escaped from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”

5But he shook the creature into the fire and suffered no harm.

6They expected him to swell up or suddenly fall down dead. After waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said that he was a god.

7Near that place were lands belonging to the island’s chief man, named Publius. He welcomed us and hospitably gave us lodging for three days.

8Publius’s father lay sick with fevers and dysentery. Paul went in to him, prayed, laid his hands upon him, and healed him.

9After this happened, the other sick people on the island also came and were healed.

10They honored us with many honors, and when we sailed, they supplied what we needed.

11After three months we sailed in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered at the island, with the Dioscuri as its emblem.

12We put in at Syracuse and stayed three days.

13From there we cast off and reached Rhegium. After one day a south wind arose, and on the second day we came to Puteoli.

14There we found brothers and were invited to stay with them seven days. And so we came to Rome.

15From there the brothers, having heard about us, came to meet us as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.

16When we entered Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself with the soldier guarding him.

17After three days he called together the leading Jews. When they gathered, he said to them, “Men, brothers, although I had done nothing against the people or the ancestral customs, I was handed over as a prisoner from Jerusalem into Roman hands.

18After examining me, they wished to release me, because there was no cause for death in my case.

19But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, though I had no accusation to bring against my nation.

20For this reason I asked to see you and speak with you, for it is because of Israel’s hope that I wear this chain.”

21They said to him, “We have received no letters from Judea about you, nor has any of the brothers who arrived reported or spoken anything evil about you.

22But we consider it right to hear from you what you think, for concerning this sect we know that it is opposed everywhere.”

23They appointed a day with him and came to his lodging in greater numbers. From morning until evening he explained to them, bearing solemn witness to the kingdom of God and seeking to persuade them concerning Jesus from both the law of Moses and the prophets.

24Some were persuaded by what was said, while others did not believe.

25Disagreeing with one another, they began to leave after Paul made one statement: “The Holy Spirit spoke well through Isaiah the prophet to your fathers,

26saying, ‘Go to this people and say: “You will hear and hear, yet never understand; you will look and look, yet never see.

27For this people’s heart has grown dull, their ears have become hard of hearing, and they have closed their eyes, lest they see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn back, and I would heal them.”’

28Therefore let it be known to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles; they will listen.”

30He remained two whole years in his own rented lodging and welcomed all who came to him,

31proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, unhindered.

Romans 1

1Paul, a slave of Christ Jesus, called as an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,

2which He promised beforehand through His prophets in holy Scriptures,

3concerning His Son, who came from David’s seed according to the flesh,

4who was designated Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness by resurrection from the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,

5through whom we received grace and apostleship for the obedience of faith among all the nations for His name,

6among whom you also are, called by Jesus Christ:

7to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called as saints: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

8First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is proclaimed in the whole world.

9For God, whom I serve in my spirit in the gospel of His Son, is my witness that I remember you without ceasing,

10always in my prayers asking whether somehow now at last I may be granted a way, by the will of God, to come to you.

11For I long to see you, to share with you some spiritual gift so that you may be strengthened,

12that is, to be encouraged together among you through one another’s faith, both yours and mine.

13And I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that I often planned to come to you—and was hindered until now—so that I might have some fruit among you also, just as among the other nations.

14I am a debtor both to Greeks and to those who do not speak Greek, both to the wise and to the senseless.

15Thus, for my part, I am eager to proclaim the gospel also to you who are in Rome.

16For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is God’s power for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.

17For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith, as it is written, “But the righteous one will live by faith.”

18For God’s wrath is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of people who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,

19because what is known of God is plain among them, for God made it plain to them.

20For His invisible qualities, both His eternal power and divinity, have been clearly seen since the creation of the world, understood through the things made, so that they are without excuse,

21because, although they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God or give thanks, but became futile in their thoughts, and their senseless heart was darkened.

22Claiming to be wise, they became foolish,

23and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible humanity, and of birds and four-footed animals and creeping things.

24Therefore God handed them over, in the desires of their hearts, to impurity, so that their bodies would be dishonored among them,

25who exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and revered and worshiped the creation instead of the Creator, who is blessed throughout the ages. Amen.

26For this reason God handed them over to dishonorable passions; for their females exchanged natural relations for those contrary to nature,

27and likewise the males, leaving natural relations with the female, burned in their desire for one another, males with males committing what is shameful and receiving in themselves the due penalty for their error.

28And just as they did not see fit to retain God in their knowledge, God handed them over to an unfit mind, to do what is not fitting:

29filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, evil; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, malice; whisperers,

30slanderers, haters of God, insolent, proud, boastful, inventors of evils, disobedient to parents,

31without understanding, faithless, without natural affection, merciless;

32who, knowing God’s righteous decree, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, not only do them, but also approve those who practice them.

6who will repay each according to his works:

10but glory and honor and peace to everyone who does good, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.

11For there is no partiality with God.

28For the Jew is not the one outwardly so, nor is circumcision what is outward in flesh;

29but the Jew is the one inwardly so, and circumcision is of the heart, in Spirit, not in letter, whose praise is not from people but from God.

Faith in Christ or Christ’s faithfulness?

The inherited reading “faith in Jesus Christ” is retained provisionally. “Faithfulness of Jesus Christ” is another interpretation of the genitive relationship; the case ending alone does not settle it.

The sentence also names all who believe. This provides relevant context but does not mechanically eliminate the competing interpretation of the preceding phrase.

  • faithfulness of Jesus Christ — Changes whose faithfulness the phrase directly describes; requires argument from usage and context.

Do not blend both readings into an expanded Scripture sentence. A specialist lexical and syntactic review remains open.

The sacrificial term in Romans 3:25

“Propitiation” is retained from the inherited draft while its precise English rendering remains under review. Proposals such as “means of expiation” or “mercy seat” reflect different readings of the sacrificial language.

Blood, faith, the demonstration of God's righteousness, and the passing over of previous sins form the immediate argument. Their grammatical attachments must be considered along with the noun.

Romans 5

1Therefore, having been justified from faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,

2through whom we have also obtained access by faith into this grace in which we stand; and we boast in hope of God’s glory.

3And not only this, but we also boast in afflictions, knowing that affliction produces perseverance,

4and perseverance, proven character, and proven character, hope.

5And hope does not put us to shame, because God’s love has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.

6For while we were still weak, even then Christ died at the appointed time for the ungodly.

7For rarely will someone die for a righteous person; though perhaps for the good person someone even dares to die.

8But God demonstrates His own love toward us in that, while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

9Much more, then, having now been justified in His blood, we will be saved through Him from wrath.

10For if, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son, much more, having been reconciled, we will be saved in His life.

11And not only this, but we also boast in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.

12For this reason, just as through one person sin entered the world, and through sin, death, and so death passed to all people, because all sinned—

13for before the law came, sin was in the world, but sin is not charged to account when there is no law;

14nevertheless death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the likeness of Adam’s transgression, who is a type of the One to come.

15But the gift is not like the trespass. For if by the one man’s trespass the many died, much more did God’s grace and the gift in the grace of the one Man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many.

16And the gift is not like what came through one who sinned; for the judgment from one trespass resulted in condemnation, but the gift from many trespasses resulted in justification.

17For if, by the one man’s trespass, death reigned through the one, much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness reign in life through the One, Jesus Christ.

18So then, as through one trespass there was condemnation for all people, so also through one righteous act there is justification of life for all people.

19For just as through the disobedience of the one person the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the One the many will be made righteous.

20But law came in alongside, so that the trespass might increase; but where sin increased, grace abounded beyond measure,

21so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness for eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

Romans 6

1What, then, shall we say? Should we remain in sin so that grace may increase?

2May it never be! We who died to sin, how will we still live in it?

3Or do you not know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?

4Therefore we were buried with Him through baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the Father’s glory, so we also might walk in newness of life.

5For if we have become united with the likeness of His death, we will also be united with that of His resurrection,

6knowing this, that our old self was crucified with Him, so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, so that we would no longer be enslaved to sin;

7for the one who died has been justified from sin.

8And if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him,

9knowing that Christ, having been raised from the dead, no longer dies; death no longer rules over Him.

10For the death He died, He died to sin once for all; but the life He lives, He lives to God.

11So also reckon yourselves to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.

12Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body, so that you obey its desires;

13Do not present the parts of your body to sin as weapons of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and the parts of your body to God as weapons of righteousness.

14For sin will not rule over you, for you are not under law, but under grace.

15What, then? Should we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? May it never be!

16Do you not know that when you present yourselves to someone as slaves to obey, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin leading to death, or of obedience leading to righteousness?

17But thanks be to God that, though you were slaves of sin, you obeyed from the heart the pattern of teaching to which you were handed over;

18and, having been set free from sin, you were enslaved to righteousness.

19I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. For just as you presented the parts of your body as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness leading to lawlessness, so now present the parts of your body as slaves to righteousness leading to sanctification.

20For when you were slaves of sin, you were free from righteousness.

21What fruit, then, did you have at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of those things is death.

22But now, having been set free from sin and enslaved to God, you have your fruit leading to sanctification, and the end, eternal life.

23For sin’s wages are death, but God’s gift is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Romans 7

1Or do you not know, brothers—for I speak to those who know law—that the law rules over a person for as long as he lives?

2For the married woman is bound by law to her living husband; but if the husband dies, she has been released from the law of the husband.

3So then, while the husband lives, she will be called an adulteress if she belongs to another man; but if the husband dies, she is free from the law, so that she is not an adulteress when she belongs to another man.

4So, my brothers, you also were put to death to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might belong to Another, the One raised from the dead, so that we might bear fruit for God.

5For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions aroused through the law were at work in the parts of our body, to bear fruit for death.

6But now we were released from the law, having died to that in which we were held, so that we serve in the newness of the Spirit and not in the oldness of the letter.

7What, then, shall we say? Is the law sin? May it never be! Rather, I did not know sin except through law; for I would not have known desire if the law had not said, “You shall not desire.”

8But sin, taking opportunity through the commandment, produced every desire in me; for apart from law sin is dead.

9And I was once alive apart from law; but when the commandment came, sin came to life,

10and I died; and the commandment that was for life proved to bring me death.

11For sin, taking opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me.

12So the law is holy, and the commandment holy and righteous and good.

13Did the good, then, become death to me? May it never be! But sin did, so that it might appear as sin, producing death in me through the good, so that through the commandment sin might become sinful beyond measure.

14For we know that the law is spiritual; but I am of flesh, sold under sin.

15For I do not understand what I do; for I do not practice what I want, but what I hate, this I do.

16But if I do what I do not want, I agree with the law that it is good.

17But now it is no longer I who do it, but sin dwelling in me.

18For I know that good does not dwell in me—that is, in my flesh. For the will is there, but doing what is good is not.

19For I do not do the good that I want, but the evil that I do not want, this I practice.

20But if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but sin dwelling in me.

21So I find this law: when I want to do the good, evil is at hand for me.

22For I delight in God’s law in my inner self,

23but I see another law in the parts of my body, waging war against the law of my mind and taking me captive in the law of sin that is in the parts of my body.

24Wretched person that I am! Who will rescue me from the body of this death?

25Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then I myself, with the mind, serve God’s law, but with the flesh, sin’s law.

Romans 8

1So then, there is now no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus.

2For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus set you free from the law of sin and death.

3For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God did: sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and concerning sin, He condemned sin in the flesh,

4so that the law’s righteous requirement might be fulfilled in us who walk not according to flesh, but according to Spirit.

5For those who are according to flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those according to Spirit, on the things of the Spirit.

6For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace,

7because the mind of the flesh is hostility toward God; for it does not submit to God’s law, nor indeed can it.

8And those who are in flesh cannot please God.

9But you are not in flesh, but in Spirit, if indeed God’s Spirit dwells in you. But if anyone does not have Christ’s Spirit, that person does not belong to Him.

10But if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the Spirit is life because of righteousness.

11And if the Spirit of the One who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, the One who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit dwelling in you.

12So then, brothers, we are debtors—not to the flesh, to live according to flesh;

13for if you live according to flesh, you are going to die; but if by Spirit you put to death the body’s practices, you will live.

14For all who are led by God’s Spirit are sons of God.

15For you did not receive a spirit of slavery leading again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption as sons, in whom we cry, “Abba, Father.”

16The Spirit Himself bears witness with our spirit that we are God’s children.

17And if children, then also heirs: heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer with Him so that we may also be glorified with Him.

18For I reckon that the sufferings of the present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed in us.

19For creation eagerly awaits the revealing of God’s sons;

20for creation was subjected to futility, not willingly, but because of the One who subjected it, in hope

21that creation itself also will be set free from slavery to corruption into the freedom of the glory of God’s children.

22For we know that the whole creation groans together and labors in birth pangs together until now;

23and not only creation, but we ourselves also, having the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan within ourselves, awaiting adoption as sons, the redemption of our body.

24For in hope we were saved. But hope that is seen is not hope; for who hopes for what he sees?

25But if we hope for what we do not see, we await it with perseverance.

26And likewise the Spirit also helps our weakness; for we do not know what to pray for as we ought, but the Spirit Himself intercedes with groanings beyond words.

27And the One who searches hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because He intercedes for saints according to God.

28And we know that all things work together for good for those who love God, those who are called according to purpose.

29Because those whom He foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He might be firstborn among many brothers;

30and those whom He predestined, these He also called; and those whom He called, these He also justified; and those whom He justified, these He also glorified.

31What, then, shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?

32He who did not spare His own Son, but handed Him over for us all, how will He not also graciously give us all things with Him?

33Who will bring a charge against God’s chosen ones? God is the One who justifies.

34Who is the one who condemns? Christ Jesus is the One who died—more than that, was raised—who is also at God’s right hand, who also intercedes for us.

35Who will separate us from Christ’s love? Affliction, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?

36Just as it is written, “For Thy sake we are put to death all day long; we were reckoned as sheep for slaughter.”

37But in all these things we more than conquer through the One who loved us.

38For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor rulers, neither things present nor things to come nor powers,

39neither height nor depth nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Romans 9

1I speak truth in Christ; I do not lie, my conscience bearing witness with me in the Holy Spirit,

2that I have great sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart.

3For I could wish that I myself were accursed, away from Christ, for the sake of my brothers, my kinsmen according to the flesh,

4who are Israelites. Theirs are the adoption as sons and the glory and the covenants and the giving of the law and the worship and the promises;

5theirs are the fathers, and from them comes the Christ according to the flesh, who is over all, God blessed throughout the ages. Amen.

6But it is not as though God’s word has failed. For not all who are from Israel are Israel;

7neither, because they are Abraham’s seed, are they all children; but, “In Isaac your seed will be called.”

8That is, the children of the flesh are not thereby God’s children, but the children of the promise are reckoned as seed.

9For this is a word of promise: “At this time I will come, and Sarah will have a son.”

10And not only this, but also Rebecca, having conceived by one man, Isaac our father—

11for when they had not yet been born or done anything good or bad, so that God’s purpose according to election might remain,

12not from works but from the One who calls, it was said to her, “The older will serve the younger,”

13just as it is written, “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”

14What, then, shall we say? Is there unrighteousness with God? May it never be!

15For He says to Moses, “I will have mercy on whomever I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whomever I have compassion.”

16So then, it depends not on the one who wills, nor on the one who runs, but on God who has mercy.

17For the Scripture says to Pharaoh, “For this very purpose I raised you up, so that I might demonstrate My power in you, and so that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”

18So then, He has mercy on whom He wills, and whom He wills He hardens.

19You will then say to me, “Why, then, does He still find fault? For who has resisted His purpose?”

20But who are you, O man, to answer back to God? Will what is formed say to the One who formed it, “Why didst Thou make me this way?”

21Or does the potter not have authority over the clay, from the same lump to make one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?

22But what if God, willing to demonstrate wrath and to make His power known, endured with much patience vessels of wrath fitted for destruction,

23and did so to make known the wealth of His glory upon vessels of mercy, which He prepared beforehand for glory,

24even us whom He also called, not only from Jews but also from Gentiles?

25As He also says in Hosea, “I will call those who are not My people ‘My people,’ and her who is not beloved ‘beloved’;

26and it shall come to pass that in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ there they will be called sons of the living God.”

27But Isaiah cries out concerning Israel, “Though the number of Israel’s sons be like the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved;

28for the Lord will carry out a word on the earth, completing it and cutting it short.”

29And just as Isaiah has said beforehand, “Unless the Lord Sabaoth had left us seed, we would have become like Sodom and would have been made like Gomorrah.”

30What, then, shall we say? That Gentiles who were not pursuing righteousness attained righteousness, namely the righteousness from faith;

31but Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness, did not attain law.

32Why? Because it was not from faith, but as though from works. They stumbled against the stone of stumbling,

33just as it is written, “Behold, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, and the one who believes in Him will not be put to shame.”

Romans 10

1Brothers, my heart’s desire and my prayer to God for them are that they may be saved.

2For I bear them witness that they have zeal for God, but not according to knowledge;

3for, not knowing God’s righteousness and seeking to establish their own righteousness, they did not submit to God’s righteousness.

4For Christ is the end of law for righteousness to everyone who believes.

5For Moses writes about the righteousness from the law: the person who does these things will live by them.

6But the righteousness from faith speaks in this way: “Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’”—that is, to bring Christ down;

7or, “‘Who will descend into the abyss?’”—that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.

8But what does it say? “The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart”—that is, the word of faith that we proclaim.

9Because if you confess Jesus as Lord with your mouth, and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved;

10for with the heart one believes for righteousness, and with the mouth one confesses for salvation.

11For the Scripture says, “Whoever believes in Him shall not be put to shame.”

12For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek, for the same Lord is Lord of all, being rich toward all who call upon Him;

13for “everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.”

14How, then, are they to call upon One in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in One whom they have not heard? And how are they to hear without someone proclaiming?

15And how are they to proclaim unless they are sent? Just as it is written, “How beautiful are the feet of those announcing good things!”

16But not all obeyed the gospel. For Isaiah says, “O Lord, who has believed our report?”

17So faith is from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ.

18But I say, did they not hear? Indeed they did: “Their sound went out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the inhabited world.”

19But I say, did Israel not know? First Moses says, “I will make you jealous by what is not a nation; by a senseless nation I will provoke you to anger.”

20And Isaiah speaks boldly and says, “I was found among those who did not seek Me; I became known to those who did not ask for Me.”

21But concerning Israel He says, “All day long I stretched out My hands toward a disobedient and contrary people.”

Romans 11

1I say, then, has God rejected His people? May it never be! For I too am an Israelite, from Abraham’s seed, of Benjamin’s tribe.

2God has not rejected His people whom He foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says in the passage about Elijah, how he pleads with God against Israel?

3“Lord, they killed Thy prophets, they demolished Thy altars, and I alone was left, and they seek my life.”

4But what does the divine response say to him? “I left for Myself seven thousand men who did not bend the knee to Baal.”

5So then, at the present time also there has come to be a remnant according to an election of grace.

6But if by grace, it is no longer from works; otherwise grace is no longer grace.

7What, then? What Israel seeks, it did not obtain; but the chosen obtained it, and the rest were hardened,

8just as it is written, “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes not to see and ears not to hear, until this very day.”

9And David says, “Let their table become a snare and a trap and a stumbling block and a repayment to them;

10let their eyes be darkened so as not to see, and bend their back continually.”

11I say, then, did they stumble so that they might fall? May it never be! But by their trespass salvation has come to the Gentiles, to make them jealous.

12But if their trespass is the world’s wealth and their loss the Gentiles’ wealth, how much more their fullness!

13And I speak to you Gentiles. Insofar as I am an apostle of Gentiles, I glorify my ministry,

14if somehow I may make my own flesh jealous and save some of them.

15For if their rejection is the world’s reconciliation, what will their acceptance be except life from the dead?

16And if the firstfruits are holy, so is the lump; and if the root is holy, so are the branches.

17But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them and came to share in the olive tree’s rich root,

18do not boast over the branches. But if you boast, it is not you who bear the root, but the root bears you.

19You will then say, “Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.”

20Well: they were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not be haughty, but fear;

21for if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will He spare you.

22See, then, God’s kindness and severity: severity upon those who fell, but God’s kindness upon you, if you remain in the kindness; otherwise you too will be cut off.

23And they also, if they do not remain in unbelief, will be grafted in; for God is able to graft them in again.

24For if you were cut from what is by nature a wild olive, and contrary to nature were grafted into a cultivated olive, how much more will these natural branches be grafted into their own olive tree!

25For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of this mystery, so that you may not be wise in your own eyes: that a partial hardening has come upon Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles enters,

26and in this way all Israel will be saved, just as it is written: “The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.

27And this is My covenant with them, when I take away their sins.”

28With regard to the gospel, they are enemies for your sake; but with regard to election, beloved for the fathers’ sake.

29For God’s gifts and calling are irrevocable.

30For just as you once disobeyed God, but now received mercy through their disobedience,

31so they also now disobeyed, so that through the mercy shown to you they also may now receive mercy.

32For God confined all in disobedience so that He might have mercy on all.

33O depth of God’s wealth and wisdom and knowledge! How unsearchable His judgments and untraceable His ways!

34“For who knew the Lord’s mind? Or who became His counselor?

35Or who gave to Him first, and it will be repaid to him?”

36Because from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory throughout the ages. Amen.

Romans 12

1Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God—your rational worship.

2And do not be conformed to this age, but be transformed by the renewal of the mind, so that you may discern what God’s will is: the good and pleasing and perfect.

3For through the grace given me I say to everyone among you not to think more highly than one ought to think, but to think with sound judgment, as God apportioned to each a measure of faith.

4For as we have many parts in one body, and the parts do not all have the same function,

5so we, the many, are one body in Christ, and each one is a member of the others.

6And since we have gifts differing according to the grace given to us: if prophecy, let it be according to the proportion of faith;

7if service, in serving; if one teaches, in teaching;

8if one exhorts, in exhortation; the one who shares, with generosity; the one who leads, with diligence; the one who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.

9Let love be without hypocrisy. Abhor what is evil; cling to what is good.

10In brotherly love be tenderly devoted to one another; take the lead in honoring one another;

11do not be slack in zeal; be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord;

12rejoice in hope; persevere in affliction; persist in prayer;

13share in the needs of the saints; pursue hospitality.

14Bless those who persecute you; bless, and do not curse.

15Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.

16Have the same mind toward one another. Do not set your minds on lofty things, but associate with the lowly. Do not become wise in your own eyes.

17Repay no one evil for evil. Take thought for what is honorable before all people.

18If possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with all people.

19Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but make room for wrath; for it is written, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”

20But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head.

21Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.

Romans 13

1Let every soul submit to the higher authorities, for there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been appointed by God.

2Therefore the one who sets himself against authority has resisted God’s ordering, and those who resist will receive judgment upon themselves.

3For rulers are not a terror to good work, but to evil. Do you want to be free from fear of the authority? Do the good, and you will have praise from it;

4for it is God’s servant to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid; for it does not bear the sword without purpose. For it is God’s servant, an avenger who brings wrath on the one who practices evil.

5Therefore it is necessary to submit, not only because of wrath, but also because of conscience.

6For this reason you also pay taxes, for they are God’s ministers, devoted to this very task.

7Pay everyone what is owed: tax to whom tax is due, duty to whom duty is due, fear to whom fear is due, honor to whom honor is due.

8Owe no one anything except to love one another; for the one who loves the other has fulfilled law.

9For “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not desire,” and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

10Love does no evil to the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.

11And do this knowing the time, that it is already the hour for you to rise from sleep; for now salvation is nearer to us than when we believed.

12The night has advanced, and the day has drawn near. Therefore let us put away the works of darkness and put on the weapons of light.

13Let us walk honorably as in daytime, not in revelries and drunkenness, not in sexual promiscuity and licentiousness, not in strife and jealousy;

14but put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not make provision for the flesh to satisfy its desires.

Romans 14

1Welcome the one who is weak in faith, but not to dispute over opinions.

2One believes he may eat all things, but the weak person eats vegetables.

3Do not let the one who eats despise the one who does not eat; and do not let the one who does not eat judge the one who eats, for God welcomed him.

4Who are you to judge another’s household slave? To his own master he stands or falls; and he will be made to stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.

5For one judges one day above another, but another judges every day alike. Let each be fully assured in his own mind.

6The one who regards the day regards it for the Lord. And the one who eats eats for the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and the one who does not eat refrains for the Lord and gives thanks to God.

7For none of us lives for himself, and none dies for himself;

8for if we live, we live for the Lord, and if we die, we die for the Lord. So whether we live or die, we are the Lord’s.

9For to this end Christ died and lived, so that He might be Lord of both the dead and the living.

10But why do you judge your brother? Or you also, why do you despise your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat,

11for it is written, “As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bend to Me, and every tongue will confess to God.”

12So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.

13Therefore let us no longer judge one another; but judge this instead: not to place a stumbling block or a snare for a brother.

14I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself; except that to the one who reckons something unclean, to that person it is unclean.

15For if your brother is grieved because of food, you no longer walk according to love. Do not destroy with your food the one for whom Christ died.

16Therefore do not let your good be spoken of as evil.

17For God’s kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit;

18for the one who serves Christ in this is pleasing to God and approved by people.

19So then, let us pursue what makes for peace and what builds up one another.

20Do not tear down God’s work for the sake of food. All things indeed are clean, but it is evil for a person to eat in a way that causes stumbling.

21It is good not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything by which your brother stumbles.

22The faith you have, keep to yourself before God. Blessed is the one who does not judge himself in what he approves.

23But the one who doubts, if he eats, has been condemned, because it is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.

Romans 15

1And we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of those without strength, and not to please ourselves.

2Let each of us please our neighbor for his good, to build him up.

3For even Christ did not please Himself; but just as it is written, “The reproaches of those who reproach Thee fell upon Me.”

4For whatever was written beforehand was written for our instruction, so that through perseverance and through the encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.

5And may the God of perseverance and encouragement grant you to have the same mind among one another according to Christ Jesus,

6so that with one accord and one mouth you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

7Therefore welcome one another, just as Christ also welcomed you, to God’s glory.

8For I say that Christ has become a servant of the circumcision for God’s truth, to confirm the promises of the fathers,

9and for the Gentiles to glorify God for mercy, just as it is written, “For this reason I will give thanks to Thee among the Gentiles, and sing praise to Thy name.”

10And again it says, “Rejoice, Gentiles, with His people.”

11And again, “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and let all the peoples praise Him.”

12And again Isaiah says, “There will be the root of Jesse, and the One who rises to rule Gentiles; upon Him Gentiles will hope.”

13And may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope in the power of the Holy Spirit.

14And I myself am convinced about you, my brothers, that you yourselves also are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish one another.

15But I wrote more boldly to you on some points, to remind you again, because of the grace given me by God

16to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, performing priestly service with God’s gospel, so that the offering of the Gentiles may become acceptable, sanctified in the Holy Spirit.

17Therefore I have reason to boast in Christ Jesus concerning the things of God;

18for I will not dare to speak of anything that Christ did not work through me for the Gentiles’ obedience, in word and deed,

19in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Spirit of God, so that from Jerusalem and around as far as Illyricum I have fulfilled the proclamation of Christ’s gospel,

20and so making it my ambition to proclaim the gospel where Christ has not been named, so that I would not build on another’s foundation,

21but just as it is written, “Those to whom nothing about Him was announced will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”

22For this reason I was also often hindered from coming to you;

23but now, no longer having a place in these regions, and having a longing for many years to come to you,

24whenever I travel to Spain—for I hope to see you as I pass through, and to be sent onward there by you, if I may first be filled in some measure by your company—

25but now I am traveling to Jerusalem, serving the saints.

26For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.

27For they were pleased, and they are their debtors; for if the Gentiles shared in their spiritual things, they also owe them service in material things.

28Therefore, having completed this and sealed this fruit for them, I will depart by way of you for Spain.

29And I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of Christ’s blessing.

30And I urge you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to struggle together with me in prayers to God for me,

31so that I may be rescued from those who disobey in Judea, and my service for Jerusalem may become acceptable to the saints,

32so that, coming to you in joy through God’s will, I may find rest together with you.

33And may the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

1And I commend to you Phoebe our sister, who is also a deacon of the Church in Cenchreae,

2so that you may welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and stand by her in whatever matter she may need from you; for she herself has been a patron of many, and of me personally.

3Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,

4who risked their own neck for my life, to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the Churches of the Gentiles;

5and greet the Church in their house. Greet Epaenetus my beloved, who is the firstfruits of Asia for Christ.

6Greet Mary, who labored much for you.

7Greet Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen and fellow prisoners, who are distinguished among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.

8Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.

9Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and Stachys my beloved.

10Greet Apelles, approved in Christ. Greet those of Aristobulus’s household.

11Greet Herodion my kinsman. Greet those of Narcissus’s household who are in the Lord.

12Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Greet Persis the beloved, who labored much in the Lord.

13Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

14Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.

15Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.

16Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the Churches of Christ greet you.

17And I urge you, brothers, to watch those who cause divisions and snares contrary to the teaching you learned, and turn away from them;

18for such people do not serve our Lord Christ, but their own belly, and through smooth speech and flattery they deceive the hearts of the unsuspecting.

19For your obedience has reached everyone; therefore I rejoice over you, but I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.

20And the God of peace will crush Satan under your feet soon. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.

21Timothy my fellow worker greets you, and Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my kinsmen.

22I, Tertius, who wrote the letter, greet you in the Lord.

23Gaius, my host and host of the whole Church, greets you. Erastus the city steward greets you, and Quartus the brother.

24[[The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.]]

1 Corinthians 1

1Paul, called as an apostle of Christ Jesus through God’s will, and Sosthenes the brother,

2to the Church of God in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus, called as saints, together with all who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, theirs and ours:

3Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

4I always thank my God for you because of the grace of God given to you in Christ Jesus,

5because in Him you were enriched in everything, in all speech and all knowledge,

6just as the testimony of Christ was confirmed among you,

7so that you lack no gift as you eagerly await the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ.

8He will also keep you firm until the end, free from accusation on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

9God is faithful, through whom you were called into the fellowship of His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

10Now I appeal to you, brothers, through the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak in agreement and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be restored to unity in the same mind and the same judgment.

11For Chloe’s people have made it clear to me, my brothers, that there are quarrels among you.

12What I mean is this: each of you says, “I belong to Paul,” or “I to Apollos,” or “I to Cephas,” or “I to Christ.”

13Has Christ been divided? Paul was not crucified for you, was he? Or were you baptized into Paul’s name?

14I give thanks to God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,

15so that no one may say that you were baptized into my own name.

16I did also baptize the household of Stephanas; beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized anyone else.

17For Christ did not send me to baptize but to proclaim the good news, without wisdom of speech, so that the cross of Christ might not be emptied of its power.

18For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is God’s power.

19For it is written, “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and I will set aside the understanding of the discerning.”

20Where is the wise person? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Has not God made the world’s wisdom foolish?

21For since, in God’s wisdom, the world did not know God through wisdom, God was pleased through the foolishness of the proclamation to save those who believe.

22For Jews ask for signs and Greeks seek wisdom,

23but we proclaim Christ crucified: a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,

24but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is God’s power and God’s wisdom.

25For God’s foolishness is wiser than human beings, and God’s weakness is stronger than human beings.

26For consider your calling, brothers: not many were wise according to the flesh, not many powerful, not many of noble birth.

27But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise, and God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong;

28and God chose the lowborn things of the world and the despised things, the things that are not, to bring to nothing the things that are,

29so that no flesh may boast before God.

30But it is from Him that you are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification and redemption,

31so that, as it is written, “Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.”

1 Corinthians 2

1And when I came to you, brothers, I did not come with lofty speech or wisdom, proclaiming to you the mystery of God.

2For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and Him crucified.

3And I was with you in weakness and in fear and in much trembling.

4My speech and my proclamation were not in persuasive words of wisdom, but in a demonstration of Spirit and power,

5so that your faith might rest in God’s power rather than human wisdom.

6Yet we speak wisdom among the mature, a wisdom belonging neither to this age nor to the rulers of this age, who are being brought to nothing.

7Instead, we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery, the hidden wisdom that God appointed beforehand, before the ages, for our glory.

8None of the rulers of this age has known it; for if they had known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

9But as it is written, “What an eye has not seen and an ear has not heard, and what has not arisen in a human heart—these are the things God prepared for those who love Him.”

10But God revealed them to us through the Spirit, for the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.

11For who among human beings knows the things of a person except the person’s spirit within? So also no one has known the things of God except the Spirit of God.

12Now we did not receive the spirit of the world but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may know the things freely given to us by God.

13We also speak these things, not in words taught by human wisdom but in those taught by the Spirit, explaining spiritual things to spiritual people.

14But a natural person does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to such a person, who cannot know them because they are discerned spiritually.

15The spiritual person discerns all things, but is himself discerned by no one.

16For “Who has known the Lord’s mind, so as to instruct Him?” But we have Christ’s mind.

1 Corinthians 3

1And I, brothers, could not speak to you as spiritual people, but as people of flesh, as infants in Christ.

2I gave you milk to drink, not solid food, for you were not yet able to receive it. Indeed, even now you are still unable,

3for you are still fleshly. For where there are jealousy and quarrels among you, are you not fleshly and walking in a merely human way?

4For whenever someone says, “I belong to Paul,” and another, “I to Apollos,” are you not merely human?

5What, then, is Apollos? And what is Paul? Servants through whom you believed, each as the Lord granted.

6I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth.

7So neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but God who gives the growth.

8The one who plants and the one who waters are one, but each will receive his own wages according to his own labor.

9For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s cultivated field, God’s building.

10According to the grace of God given to me, I laid a foundation as a wise master builder, and another builds upon it. But let each one watch how he builds upon it.

11For no one can lay another foundation besides the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.

12Now if anyone builds on the foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, grass, or straw,

13each person’s work will become clear, for the day will disclose it, because it is revealed in fire; and the fire itself will test what sort of work each has done.

14If anyone’s work that he has built upon the foundation remains, he will receive wages.

15If anyone’s work is burned up, he will suffer loss, but he himself will be saved, though in this way: as through fire.

16Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells among you?

17If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy that person. For God’s temple is holy, and that is what you are.

18Let no one deceive himself. If anyone among you thinks he is wise in this age, let him become foolish so that he may become wise.

19For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, “He catches the wise in their craftiness,”

20and again, “The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are futile.”

21So let no one boast in human beings, for all things are yours,

22whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas, or the world or life or death, or present things or things to come—all are yours,

23and you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.

1 Corinthians 4

1This is how a person should regard us: as servants of Christ and stewards of God’s mysteries.

2Moreover, what is required of stewards is that each be found faithful.

3But to me it is a very small matter that I should be examined by you or by a human court; indeed, I do not even examine myself.

4For I am aware of nothing against myself, but I am not thereby justified. The One who examines me is the Lord.

5So judge nothing before the time, until the Lord comes. He will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness and reveal the purposes of hearts; then each one’s praise will come from God.

6Now, brothers, I have applied these things figuratively to myself and Apollos for your sake, so that in us you may learn, “Not beyond what is written,” so that none of you may be puffed up in favor of one against another.

7For who makes you different? And what do you have that you did not receive? But if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you had not received it?

8Already you have your fill! Already you have become rich! Without us you have become kings! And I wish indeed that you had become kings, so that we too might reign with you.

9For I think God has displayed us apostles last of all, as people condemned to death, because we have become a spectacle to the world, both to angels and to human beings.

10We are foolish for Christ’s sake, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You are honored, but we are dishonored.

11To this very hour we hunger and thirst, are poorly clothed, are beaten, and have no settled home,

12and we toil, working with our own hands. When insulted, we bless; when persecuted, we endure;

13when slandered, we appeal. We have become like the world’s refuse, everyone’s scrapings, until now.

14I write these things not to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved children.

15For even if you have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the good news.

16Therefore I appeal to you: imitate me.

17For this reason I sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord. He will remind you of my ways in Christ Jesus, just as I teach everywhere in every Church.

18Some have become puffed up as though I were not coming to you.

19But I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will find out the power of those who are puffed up, not their talk.

20For God’s kingdom is in power, not in talk.

21What do you want? Should I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?

1 Corinthians 5

1Sexual immorality is actually reported among you, and such sexual immorality as does not occur even among the Gentiles: that someone has his father’s wife.

2And you are puffed up! Should you not instead have mourned, so that the one who did this deed might be removed from your midst?

3For although I am absent in body, I am present in spirit, and I have already passed judgment, as though present, on the one who acted in this way,

4in the name of our Lord Jesus, when you and my spirit are gathered together, with the power of our Lord Jesus,

5to hand such a person over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord.

6Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump of dough?

7Clean out the old leaven so that you may be a new lump of dough, just as you are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed.

8So let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

9I wrote to you in the letter not to associate with sexually immoral people,

10not at all meaning the sexually immoral people of this world, or the greedy and grasping, or idolaters; otherwise you would have to leave the world.

11But now I have written to you not to associate with anyone who is called a brother if he is sexually immoral or greedy or an idolater or abusive or a drunkard or grasping—not even to eat with such a person.

12For what have I to do with judging those outside? Do you not judge those inside?

13But God will judge those outside. Remove the wicked person from among yourselves.

1 Corinthians 6

1Does any of you, having a case against another, dare to seek judgment before the unrighteous and not before the saints?

2Or do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy of the smallest cases?

3Do you not know that we will judge angels, to say nothing of matters of ordinary life?

4If, then, you have cases concerning ordinary life, do you seat as judges those held in no regard in the Church?

5I say this to your shame. Is there really no wise person among you who will be able to decide his brother’s case,

6but brother goes to court against brother, and that before unbelievers?

7Indeed, then, it is already a complete defeat for you that you have lawsuits with one another. Why not instead be wronged? Why not instead be defrauded?

8But you yourselves do wrong and defraud—and do this to brothers.

9Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit God’s kingdom? Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate men, nor men who bed males,

10nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor the abusive, nor the grasping will inherit God’s kingdom.

11And some of you were these things. But you washed yourselves clean, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.

12All things are permitted to me, but not all things are beneficial. All things are permitted to me, but I will not be brought under the authority of anything.

13Foods are for the stomach, and the stomach for foods, but God will bring both it and them to an end. Yet the body is not for sexual immorality but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

14God both raised the Lord and will raise us through His power.

15Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I, then, take Christ’s members and make them members of a prostitute? May it never be!

16Or do you not know that the one who joins himself to a prostitute is one body with her? For He says, “The two will become one flesh.”

17But the one who joins himself to the Lord is one spirit with Him.

18Flee sexual immorality. Every sin that a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against his own body.

19Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? And you are not your own,

20for you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God in your body.

1 Corinthians 7

1Now concerning the things you wrote: it is good for a man not to touch a woman.

2But because of cases of sexual immorality, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.

3Let the husband fulfill his obligation to his wife, and likewise the wife to her husband.

4The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband does; likewise the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife does.

5Do not deprive one another, except perhaps by mutual agreement for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer and then be together again, so that Satan may not tempt you because of your lack of self-control.

6I say this by way of concession, not by way of command.

7I wish that all people were as I myself am. But each has his own gift from God, one in this way and another in that.

8Now I say to the unmarried and the widows: it is good for them if they remain as I am.

9But if they do not exercise self-control, let them marry, for it is better to marry than to burn.

10To the married I give this instruction—not I, but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband—

11but if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband—and a husband is not to dismiss his wife.

12To the rest I say—I, not the Lord: if any brother has an unbelieving wife and she agrees to live with him, let him not dismiss her.

13And if any woman has an unbelieving husband and he agrees to live with her, let her not dismiss her husband.

14For the unbelieving husband has been sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife has been sanctified in the brother. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but as it is they are holy.

15But if the unbelieving spouse separates, let that one separate. The brother or sister is not enslaved in such cases; God has called you in peace.

16For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?

17Only let each walk as the Lord has allotted to him, as God has called each one. This is what I direct in all the Churches.

18Was anyone called when already circumcised? Let him not undo his circumcision. Has anyone been called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.

19Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but keeping God’s commandments matters.

20Let each remain in the calling in which he was called.

21Were you called as a slave? Do not let it trouble you. But if you can indeed become free, make use of the opportunity instead.

22For the slave called in the Lord is the Lord’s freedperson; likewise the free person who was called is Christ’s slave.

23You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of human beings.

24Brothers, let each remain with God in the condition in which he was called.

25Now concerning virgins, I have no command from the Lord, but I give a judgment as one who has received mercy from the Lord to be faithful.

26I therefore think this is good because of the present distress: that it is good for a person to remain as he is.

27Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Are you released from a wife? Do not seek a wife.

28But even if you marry, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such people will have affliction in the flesh, and I would spare you.

29But I say this, brothers: the time has been shortened. From now on, let even those who have wives be as though they had none,

30and those who weep as though not weeping, and those who rejoice as though not rejoicing, and those who buy as though not possessing,

31and those who use the world as though not making full use of it. For the form of this world is passing away.

32I want you to be free from anxiety. The unmarried man is concerned about the Lord’s affairs, how he may please the Lord.

33But the married man is concerned about the world’s affairs, how he may please his wife,

34and he is divided. Both the unmarried woman and the virgin are concerned about the Lord’s affairs, so that each may be holy in both body and spirit. But the married woman is concerned about the world’s affairs, how she may please her husband.

35I say this for your own benefit, not to throw a noose over you, but for good order and undistracted devotion to the Lord.

36But if anyone thinks he is behaving improperly toward his virgin, if she is past her prime and it ought to happen in this way, let him do what he wants; he does not sin. Let them marry.

37But the one who stands firm in his heart, who is under no compulsion but has authority over his own will, and who has decided this in his own heart—to keep his own virgin—will do well.

38So the one who gives his own virgin in marriage does well, and the one who does not give her in marriage will do better.

39A wife is bound for as long as her husband lives. But if her husband falls asleep, she is free to marry whomever she wants, only in the Lord.

40But she is happier if she remains as she is, according to my judgment; and I think that I too have God’s Spirit.

1 Corinthians 8

1Now concerning food offered to idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

2If anyone thinks he has come to know something, he does not yet know as he ought to know.

3But if anyone loves God, that person has been known by Him.

4Therefore, concerning the eating of food offered to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world and that there is no God except one.

5For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth—as indeed there are many gods and many lords—

6yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things and we for Him, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and we through Him.

7But not everyone has this knowledge. Some, because they have been accustomed to the idol until now, eat the food as offered to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.

8But food will not present us favorably before God. We are no worse off if we do not eat, and no better off if we do.

9But take care that this authority of yours does not somehow become a stumbling block to the weak.

10For if someone sees you who have knowledge reclining at a meal in an idol’s temple, will not his conscience, weak as he is, be built up to eat food offered to idols?

11For through your knowledge the weak person is being destroyed, the brother for whom Christ died.

12When you sin against the brothers in this way and strike their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.

13Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat, so that I may not cause my brother to stumble.

1 Corinthians 9

1Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?

2If I am not an apostle to others, at least I am to you, for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

3This is my defense to those who examine me.

4Do we not have the right to eat and drink?

5Do we not have the right to take along a wife who is a sister, as do the other apostles and the Lord’s brothers and Cephas?

6Or do only Barnabas and I lack the right to refrain from working?

7Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit? Who shepherds a flock and does not share in the flock’s milk?

8Am I saying these things merely in a human way, or does not the law also say them?

9For in the law of Moses it is written, “You shall not muzzle an ox while it threshes.” Is it oxen that concern God,

10or does He surely say it for our sake? For it was written for our sake, because the plowman ought to plow in hope, and the thresher in hope of sharing.

11If we sowed spiritual things among you, is it too much if we reap your material things?

12If others share in this right over you, do we not all the more? But we did not use this right; instead, we bear everything so that we may put no hindrance in the way of the good news of Christ.

13Do you not know that those who perform the sacred duties eat what comes from the temple, and those who attend the altar share with the altar?

14In the same way, the Lord directed those who proclaim the good news to live from the good news.

15But I have used none of these things. Nor have I written this so that it should happen this way for me, for it would be better for me to die than—no one will empty my boast!

16For if I proclaim the good news, I have no boast, because necessity lies upon me. For woe to me if I do not proclaim the good news!

17For if I do this willingly, I have wages; but if unwillingly, I have been entrusted with a stewardship.

18What, then, are my wages? That when proclaiming the good news I may offer it without charge, so as not to make full use of my right in the good news.

19For though free from all, I enslaved myself to all, so that I might win more of them.

20To the Jews I became as a Jew, so that I might win Jews; to those under law, as under law—though I myself am not under law—so that I might win those under law;

21to those without law, as without law—though not without God’s law but within Christ’s law—so that I might win those without law.

22To the weak I became weak, so that I might win the weak. I have become all things to all people, so that by all means I might save some.

23I do all things for the sake of the good news, so that I may share in it with others.

24Do you not know that all the runners in a stadium run, but one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may obtain it.

25Everyone who competes exercises self-control in all things. They do so to receive a perishable wreath, but we an imperishable one.

26So I run in this way, not aimlessly; I box in this way, not as one beating the air.

27Instead, I pummel my body and bring it into slavery, so that, after proclaiming to others, I myself may not become disqualified.

1 Corinthians 10

1For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea,

2and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,

3and all ate the same spiritual food,

4and all drank the same spiritual drink, for they drank from a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.

5But God was not pleased with most of them, for they were strewn over the wilderness.

6Now these things became examples for us, so that we might not desire evil things as they also desired.

7Do not become idolaters, as some of them did, just as it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose to play.”

8Nor let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.

9Nor let us put Christ to the test, as some of them tested Him and were being destroyed by the serpents.

10Nor grumble, just as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer.

11These things happened to them as examples, and were written to admonish us, upon whom the ends of the ages have arrived.

12So let the one who thinks he stands take care that he does not fall.

13No temptation has seized you except what is common to humanity. But God is faithful: He will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear, but with the temptation will also provide the way out, so that you may be able to endure it.

14Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

15I speak as to wise people; judge for yourselves what I say.

16The cup of blessing that we bless—is it not participation in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break—is it not participation in the body of Christ?

17Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread.

18Consider Israel according to the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices participants in the altar?

19What, then, am I saying? That food offered to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?

20Rather, that what they sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God. And I do not want you to become participants with demons.

21You cannot drink the Lord’s cup and the cup of demons. You cannot partake of the Lord’s table and the table of demons.

22Or are we provoking the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?

23All things are permitted, but not all things are beneficial. All things are permitted, but not all things build up.

24Let no one seek his own good, but the other’s.

25Eat everything sold in the meat market without examining it for conscience’s sake,

26for “The earth is the Lord’s, and all that fills it.”

27If any of the unbelievers invites you and you want to go, eat everything set before you without examining it for conscience’s sake.

28But if someone says to you, “This has been offered in sacrifice,” do not eat it, for the sake of the one who informed you and for conscience’s sake.

29I mean not your own conscience, but the other’s. For why is my freedom judged by another conscience?

30If I partake with thanksgiving, why am I slandered for what I give thanks for?

31Therefore, whether you eat or drink or do anything, do everything for God’s glory.

32Give no cause for stumbling to Jews or Greeks or the Church of God,

33just as I too please everyone in everything, seeking not my own benefit but that of the many, so that they may be saved.
